AdminAccountView.description: An account as the admin console sees it — the full row, not the trimmed switch-target shape.
AdminAccountView.title: AdminAccountView

The opaque ``agent_id`` of the agent filling a role in this account, or null when none does.

precisely because the operator may not have deployed one yet.
AgentByRoleResponse.title: AgentByRoleResponse

AgentDisplayResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the twin rebuilds
the ``{agent_id -> AgentDisplay}`` dict the port returns.
AgentDisplayResponse.title: AgentDisplayResponse

AgentGenerationInfo.description: A persisted agent-definition generation, recorded when a new fingerprint is first seen.
AgentGenerationInfo.title: AgentGenerationInfo

AgentHealthCheckResponse.description: What the button shows. `ok` picks the icon, `detail` is rendered verbatim.
AgentHealthCheckResponse.title: AgentHealthCheckResponse

AgentIdsMatchingRequest.description:
All the selectors one authorize resolved — batched so the twin makes a single call per authorize
on this hot path. The response's ``matches`` are positionally aligned to this list.
AgentIdsMatchingRequest.title: AgentIdsMatchingRequest

AgentIdsMatchingResponse.description: One :class:`MatchingAgentIds` per request selector, in the same order.
AgentIdsMatchingResponse.title: AgentIdsMatchingResponse

AgentLabelsResponse.description:
One agent's text-coerced label bag as key/value pairs (empty when the agent is absent or
unlabelled); the twin rebuilds the ``dict`` its port form returns.
AgentLabelsResponse.title: AgentLabelsResponse

AgentMetricRow.description:
One agent's run metrics over a window: the shape both fleet leaderboards rank.

``error_rate_pct`` is a percentage (``12.5`` means 12.5%), not a 0-1 ratio, and is ``None`` when
no run in the window has finished: a window that is entirely in flight has no rate, which is a
different fact from a rate of zero. ``avg_latency_ms`` is ``None`` on the same reasoning.
Costs are emitted rounded to 6 decimals and the two derived metrics to 2, matching every other
producer over ``runs`` so the same number does not read differently on two screens.
AgentMetricRow.title: AgentMetricRow

AgentMover.description:
An agent whose average on one rubric moved against the immediately preceding window.

Movement is per rubric because that is the only comparison that means anything: an agent can
improve on `precision` while regressing on `safety`, and a blended delta would net them to
roughly nothing. Only agents evaluated in *both* windows can move — an agent with no prior
verdicts has no baseline, and reporting it as a +1.0 improvement would be an artefact of it
being new.
AgentMover.title: AgentMover

AgentPresenceResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the twin rebuilds
the ``{agent_id -> is_online}`` dict the port returns.
AgentPresenceResponse.title: AgentPresenceResponse

AgentPrincipalsRequest.description:
Optional ``agent_ids`` filter — absent lists every linked agent in the account, present narrows
to those ids (an empty list narrows to nothing, matching the in-process port).
AgentPrincipalsRequest.title: AgentPrincipalsRequest

AgentPrincipalsResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the by-principal twin
rebuilds the ``{principal_id -> AgentPrincipalRow}`` dict its port form returns.
AgentPrincipalsResponse.title: AgentPrincipalsResponse

AgentQualityRollup.description:
Per-agent quality over a window. `avg_score` is the headline human rating,
combining direct agent scores and the human scores on that agent's runs
(PRD: agent views combine direct + run scores). `graded_runs` counts the
distinct runs that carry a human quality score; `direct_count` the offline
grades on the agent itself.

The auto-grade (H1) signal is kept separate so the LLM evaluator never moves the
human numbers, and is reported **per rubric** in `llm_by_rubric` — an agent
measured on `precision` and `recall` has two averages, not one blend of them.
`avg_llm_score` is the single-number headline for a surface with room for one: the
*lowest* rubric's average, named in `avg_llm_rubric`. The weakest measurement is
the honest answer to "how is this agent doing", and with one rubric (the common
case) it is simply that rubric's average. Null/0/empty when the agent has no
auto-grades in the window.
AgentQualityRollup.title: AgentQualityRollup

AgentResolveResponse.description:
The canonical opaque ``agent_id`` an id-or-slug ref resolves to (the ref unchanged when nothing
matched — the twin returns it as-is so the caller's own lookup raises the domain 404).
AgentResolveResponse.title: AgentResolveResponse

AgentRevisionDiffResponse.description: Structured review surface for what changed between two agent-definition generations.
AgentRevisionDiffResponse.title: AgentRevisionDiffResponse

AgentScorecard.description:
One row of the Agents tab: an agent's **per-rubric averages**, plus eval volume and last eval.

Deliberately carries no single headline score (2026-07-29 revision, superseding PRD decision 9).
Averaging across rubrics dilutes exactly the signal worth escalating — a 0.20 on `safety` hides
inside a 0.64 blend with `clarity` — and it silently re-weights an agent whenever a rule is
added, with no change in the agent's behaviour. The per-evaluator breakdown is gone for the same
reason one level down: an evaluator's mean now spans whatever rubrics rules asked it for.

Built from LLM verdicts only — human grades show in the eval detail, they don't move these.
`rubrics` is empty when the agent has no LLM verdicts in the window.
AgentScorecard.title: AgentScorecard

AgentScorecardDetail.description:
The Agents drill-down: the scorecard plus that agent's evaluated runs (the same inbox rows,
scoped to this agent), each linking to the eval detail, and the two views the averages can't
give — how each rubric moved over the window (`series`) and which runs sit at its ends
(`extremes`).

Both are computed server-side from the same verdicts rather than folded on the client out of
`evals`, because `evals` is a capped list: once an agent has more graded runs than fit, a
client-side "worst run" would be the worst of a page, silently. These answer over the whole
window.
AgentScorecardDetail.title: AgentScorecardDetail

AgentSettings.description:
The platform-scope settings of one agent. Every field is optional; see the module docstring
for the merge-patch rule that makes "optional" mean *untouched*, never *cleared*.

Each field maps to a write the control plane already exposes on its own endpoint, with the same
semantics — this model is one vocabulary over them, not new behavior:

* ``labels`` — replaces the operator-set label bag (``PATCH /agents/{id}/labels``). Operator
  labels are ABAC facts a grant can select on, and they win over the ones a worker reports on
  heartbeat. An empty map clears them.
* ``role_ids`` — replaces the agent's unscoped role assignments
  (``PUT /authz/agents/{id}/roles``). Scoped grants are left alone. Removing the last owner role
  is refused, as it is on that endpoint.
* ``credential_ids`` — **ensure-present**, one of the two fields that are not a replace: the listed
  credentials are bound to the agent, and nothing is unbound. Unbinding stays an explicit call
  (``DELETE /credentials/{id}/bindings/{agent_id}``) because the bindings table records no
  origin, so a replace-set could not tell the operator's bindings from the LLM credential the
  create path binds itself.
* ``mcp_group_id`` — rebinds the gateway group (``PATCH /agents/{id}/mcp-group``); ``null``
  unbinds, absent leaves it.
* ``worker_allowlist`` — replaces the delegatable-worker declaration
  (``PATCH /agents/{id}/worker-allowlist``). An empty list clears it, meaning unrestricted.
* ``notification_sink_ids`` — **ensure-present**, the second field that is not a replace: the
  agent is subscribed to each listed sink and nothing is unsubscribed. A subscription is a row on
  the *sink*, and it records no origin, so a replace-set could not tell this agent's wizard-made
  subscription from one an operator attached through the sink itself. Unsubscribing stays the
  explicit call (``DELETE /notification-sinks/{sink_id}/subscriptions/{subscription_id}``).
AgentSettings.title: AgentSettings

AgentSettingsApplyStatus.description:
What became of one requested settings field.

Deliberately two-valued. There is no ``unchanged``: telling it apart from ``applied`` would cost
a read-before-write per field, and every write here is idempotent, so no caller can act on the
difference.
AgentSettingsApplyStatus.title: AgentSettingsApplyStatus

AgentSettingsBindingResult.description:
The outcome of binding one credential. Per-credential rather than per-field because a binding
can fail for one credential (deleted mid-call, wrong account) while the rest succeed, and a
caller needs to know *which* to retry.

Carries no ``retry`` of its own, unlike :class:`AgentSettingsSectionResult`: every entry here
retries at the same endpoint — ``POST /api/v1/credentials/{credentialId}/bindings`` with
``{"agent_id": ...}`` — so naming it per entry would repeat one constant rather than tell the
caller anything the ``credentialId`` does not already.
AgentSettingsBindingResult.title: AgentSettingsBindingResult

AgentSettingsResponse.description:
What the apply actually did, field by field.

Reported rather than merely succeeded because applying settings is multi-step with no wrapping
transaction — roles, bindings and the agent row are written by different components, over HTTP
once those are separate deployables — so "some applied, some did not" is a real server-side
state. Over HTTP the same fact rides the status code: 200 when every entry is ``applied``, 207
when any is ``failed``.

``sections`` carries one entry per requested field except the two that report per item: credential
bindings in ``bindings`` and sink subscriptions in ``subscriptions``.
AgentSettingsResponse.title: AgentSettingsResponse

AgentSettingsSectionResult.description:
The outcome of one requested settings field.

A ``failed`` entry carries the real ``error`` and the ``retry`` endpoint that applies *just this
field*, mirroring ``CreateAgentTriggerResult``: the whole call is never the right retry, because
re-sending a create rotates the agent's worker token, and re-sending a settings PATCH would
re-apply fields that already succeeded.
AgentSettingsSectionResult.title: AgentSettingsSectionResult

AgentSettingsSinkResult.description:
The outcome of subscribing the agent to one notification sink.

Per-sink for the same reason bindings are per-credential: one sink can fail (deleted mid-call,
another tenant's) while the rest succeed, and a caller needs to know *which* to retry. Carries no
``retry`` of its own — every entry retries at the same endpoint,
``POST /api/v1/notification-sinks/{sinkId}/subscriptions`` with ``{"target_type": "agent",
"target_id": ...}``, which the ``sinkId`` already identifies.
AgentSettingsSinkResult.title: AgentSettingsSinkResult

AgentTextMatchRequest.description:
An end user's raw search text, matched as a literal substring against an agent's card name and
its ``id_slug``. Escaping LIKE metacharacters is the port's job, not the caller's, so the text
crosses the wire exactly as it was typed.
AgentTextMatchRequest.title: AgentTextMatchRequest

AllocationStatsRequest.description:
Deliberately just the documented contract — Komodor's own `stats` handler actually
validates against its sibling `rows` endpoint's request shape (a copy-paste artifact) and
would accept `order_by`/`page_size`/`pagination_token` that do nothing on an aggregate,
non-paginated response. Not carried into this API — see the endpoint inventory.
AllocationStatsRequest.title: AllocationStatsRequest

ApiKeyBoundTo.description:
What kind of principal an API key acts as. Derived from the bound principal's kind, not a
stored column — a key on a ``human`` principal is user-bound, otherwise service-account.
ApiKeyBoundTo.title: ApiKeyBoundTo

ApprovalState.description:
Where an approval stands. ``consumed`` is distinct from ``approved`` because single use is the
whole point: a granted approval that has been spent must not let the same call through twice.
ApprovalState.title: ApprovalState

ArgConditionModel.description: One condition on a tool call's arguments.
ArgConditionModel.title: ArgConditionModel

ArgOp.description:
How an argument condition compares. A closed set of operators rather than an expression
language: a condition is always ``<arg> <op> <value>``, with no composition, precedence or
negation for a reader to unpick, which is the property a security control needs and a mini-DSL
loses on its second release.

``REGEX`` is the one operator whose *value* is itself expressive. It is here because the
conditions operators actually ask for — a ``DROP`` of any table, an ARN outside their own
account — are not reachable by glob, and the alternative was authors approximating them with
``contains`` and getting a broader rule than they read. It carries a cost the others do not: a
pattern can be slow enough to matter, so it is compiled where it is authored and bounded where it
is evaluated (see :func:`_regex_holds`).
ArgOp.title: ArgOp

AuditAction.description:
Well-known action keys for the identity/admin actions this feature records. The ``action``
column is an open string (the authz engine adds many more, e.g. ``agent.invoke``); these are the
ones defined here.
AuditAction.title: AuditAction

AuditSortKey.description:
Allow-listed columns the Audit page may sort by. Only these map to a real (indexed-friendly)
ordering expression — an arbitrary client string can never reach the ``ORDER BY``, so this is
also the injection guard for server-side sort.
AuditSortKey.title: AuditSortKey

AuditStatus.description: The action outcome. A DB-CHECK source of truth on ``audit_log`` / ``authz_decision_log``.
AuditStatus.title: AuditStatus

AuthSource.description: What the IdP / auth method asserts about this session — for display/debug, not authz.
AuthSource.title: AuthSource

AuthUser.description: The identity-spine user — the global login identity.
AuthUser.title: AuthUser

AuthzContext.description:
The caller's authorization view — a "display extra" (like ``is_system_admin``) hydrated only on
the ``/auth/me`` path, for nav-gating admin affordances. The server still enforces every action
per-resource; this is UX only.

``capabilities`` is the coarse, deduped set of capability keys the acting principal holds anywhere
in the active account (no resource scope). ``mode`` is this caller's resolved ``EnforcementMode``
string value ``"off"``/``"shadow"``/``"enforce"`` (typed as ``str`` to keep the identity module
free of an authz import, which would cycle): the UI must gate nav **only** when
``mode == "enforce"`` — under off/shadow the server allows everything, so hiding tabs would be
wrong (see #953).
AuthzContext.title: AuthzContext

AuthzMember.description: A member row for the list / attribute-edit views — adds the user-managed ABAC attributes.
AuthzMember.title: AuthzMember

AuthzServiceAccount.description: A service-account row for the list / attribute-edit views — adds ABAC attributes.
AuthzServiceAccount.title: AuthzServiceAccount

AuthzServiceAccountRoles.description: A service account's role-assignment result (what ``PUT …/service-accounts/{id}/roles`` returns).
AuthzServiceAccountRoles.title: AuthzServiceAccountRoles

AutoScoreSeries.description:
Ordered per-run auto-grade (LLM) quality values for one agent over a window,
oldest first. The Quality Lab saturation view computes a running mean ± SEM from
this flat series client-side to show whether the agent's average auto-score has
stabilized as auto-evals accumulated.

The series covers exactly ONE rubric, named in `rubric` — a running mean over
values that measure different things converges on nothing, so mixing rubrics here
would make the saturation view meaningless rather than merely imprecise. When the
caller names no rubric, the agent's lowest-averaging one is used; `rubric` is null
only when the series is empty.
AutoScoreSeries.title: AutoScoreSeries

BacktestGuardrailRequest.description:
The rule to replay. Unsaved by design — the point is to look before committing — so this takes
the same fields as a create and stores nothing.

``pattern`` criteria only. Replaying a judged one means asking a model about every historical call in
the window: minutes of latency and a bill, for an answer that is not reproducible the way a pattern's
is. The narrower model is what makes the refusal a schema error a caller can read rather than a
surprise at the far end of a slow request.
BacktestGuardrailRequest.title: BacktestGuardrailRequest

BacktestHitResponse.description:
One (agent, tool) pair the rule covers, and how often it was called.

Deliberately **no arguments**. A rule may be *decided* by them, but a tool argument can carry a
credential, which is why neither the gateway's audit trail nor a guardrail decision stores one —
and echoing them into an authoring screen would be the same leak with a nicer font.
BacktestHitResponse.title: BacktestHitResponse

CancelSignal.description:
What became of the stop-signal a cancel owed the worker holding the run.

**The database flip always succeeds; reaching the worker is a separate fact.** A cancelled run's row is
terminal either way, and a worker that never hears about it goes on burning until it finishes and then
has its report discarded. That is the honest outcome for an unreachable worker — but it was previously
said only in a log line, so the operator's cancel was answered identically whether or not it landed.
Now the answer carries it, because the follow-up differs: `undeliverable` is the one that means *this
agent is still working and will not stop*.

Four values rather than a bool, because each names a different next action. A local push and a bounce to
the owning pod are deliberately **one** value: both hand the frame to the transport that owns the worker,
and no caller can act on which.
CancelSignal.title: CancelSignal

CancelledRun.description:
What ``POST /runs/{run_id}/cancel`` answers: the cancelled run, and what became of the stop signal.

**A subclass rather than a wrapper**, deliberately. Every existing consumer of that route reads a
``RunSummary`` and keeps working — the field is additive on the wire and additive in the type, so no
caller has to be changed to keep doing what it did. A ``{run, signal}`` envelope would have been a
breaking change to say one more thing.

The one field is the fact the route could not previously report: an operator cancelling a claimed run
got the same answer whether the worker heard about it or not. See :class:`CancelSignal`.

**The three inherited ``title=``s are re-declared, and that is not cosmetic.** ``openapi-python-client``
keys its generated model files on those titles, so a second schema carrying ``RunInput`` /
``RunMetadata`` / ``RunOutput`` makes each one ambiguous — the generator hoists them into shared models
and the reshuffle propagates: adding this class without the overrides silently dropped the `200` response
body from seven *unrelated* generated endpoints and failed to emit ``GradeContext`` at all. Distinct
titles keep the generated surface additive, which is the same property the subclass exists for.
CancelledRun.title: CancelledRun

CatalogTool.description:
One upstream tool in the persisted catalog snapshot.

``name`` is the gateway-exposed namespaced name (``"<namespace>_<bare>"``);
``bare_name`` is the unprefixed name on the upstream. Carries enough schema to
reconstruct the MCP wire form without re-querying upstreams.

bare_name.description: Unprefixed tool name on the upstream server.
bare_name.title: Bare Name

name.description: Namespaced tool name as exposed by the gateway.
name.title: Name

namespace.description: Owning server's name; the mount namespace.
namespace.title: Namespace

parameters.description: JSON schema for the tool's input.
parameters.title: Parameters

CatalogTool.title: CatalogTool

ChangesRequest.description:
Window and optional agent facet for the fleet-wide deployment-change count.

``window_days`` is calendar-day inclusive (``1`` is today alone), the same form the run-activity
reads use, so the Changes tile and the tiles beside it describe one period.
ChangesRequest.title: ChangesRequest

ChangesResponse.description:
How many agent versions were deployed in the window.

Counts generations, including an agent's first — a first deploy is a deployment. It also counts
dual-deploy shadow generations: the ledger carries no arm column, and the only signal that could
exclude them lives on a replica row that its worker overwrites when it rolls forward, so the
exclusion would decay and the same window would return different numbers on different days.
ChangesResponse.title: ChangesResponse

ClusterInstallCredential.description:
The credential, in the clear, exactly once. It exists in this form at create and at rotate and
nowhere else — not in a re-read, not in an install render, not in a log line or an audit ``detail``.
ClusterInstallCredential.title: ClusterInstallCredential

ClusterInstallStatus.description:
Whether this install's declarations are enforced right now.

``PAUSED`` is the incident lever: reconciliation stops and the resources **this install owns**
become editable again in the UI and over the API. It is scoped to the install, never to the
account, so another cluster's declarations against the same account stay enforced. Resuming
reasserts declared state and therefore reverts whatever was edited while it was paused.
ClusterInstallStatus.title: ClusterInstallStatus

CodeReviewOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
CodeReviewOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: CodeReviewOnboardingCompletionResponse

ContentConditionModel.description:
One condition on a model request's content — gate #3's counterpart to :class:`ArgConditionModel`,
with a closed ``part`` in place of an argument name since a model request has no tool-defined
vocabulary to name.
ContentConditionModel.title: ContentConditionModel

CreateAgentCapabilities.description:
Operator-declared capability toggles for a self-deployed agent, mirroring the
``agentops-agent-base`` chart's ``agent.capabilities`` values block and the Add-Agent wizard's
single Chat switch.

Declaring ``chat`` advertises ``chat`` **and** ``ask``, which is what makes the agent usable from
the UI's chat surface; leaving it off makes the agent Run-only. Declaring ``review`` puts the agent
in the reviewer catalog (``code_review.reviewers``), selectable in a code-review workflow beside
the built-in reviewer.

**A capability is an advertisement, not a competence.** Nothing here can check that the agent's
prompt actually reviews code; a declared reviewer that does not review settles its reviews as a run
link with no findings, which the code-review component treats as a supported degraded tier. What
the agent is *good at* is the prompt's business.

The field set is deliberately narrow — it mirrors what the ``agentops-agent-base`` chart's
``agent.capabilities`` block can usefully carry — while the card itself stays freeform: a worker
with its own image advertises whatever its code says, and no surface validates that.
CreateAgentCapabilities.title: CreateAgentCapabilities

CreateAgentDraftRequest.description:
Create (or resume) a draft agent from the Add-Agent wizard's first step.

``agent_id`` is the operator's friendly per-account name (the id_slug); the control plane freezes
an opaque internal agent_id against it at draft-create time and returns it. ``config`` is the
opaque wizard state, persisted for cross-device resume.
CreateAgentDraftRequest.title: CreateAgentDraftRequest

CreateAgentKedaAutoscaling.description:
KEDA autoscaling for a self-deployed agent, mirroring the ``agentops-agent-base`` chart's own
``autoscaling.keda`` values block field-for-field.

**Declared intent, not an observation.** The control plane cannot see the target cluster: it does
not know whether KEDA is installed, whether the rendered ``ScaledObject`` was applied, or whether
it is reconciling. Accepting this block records what the agent was created wanting and renders it
into the returned values.yaml; it promises nothing about what the cluster actually does, and a
``helm upgrade`` outside this call silently makes it stale.
CreateAgentKedaAutoscaling.title: CreateAgentKedaAutoscaling

CreateAgentTrigger.description:
One trigger to create alongside the agent.

``name`` is optional but meaningful: it is the trigger's identity within its agent, so re-sending
the same create with a named schedule and a changed cron **updates that schedule** rather than
adding a second one. An unnamed schedule is identified by its own cron and timezone instead, which
keeps a retried request from duplicating it but offers no way to change it later — name a schedule
you expect to edit.
CreateAgentTrigger.title: CreateAgentTrigger

CreateAgentTriggerResult.description:
The outcome of one requested trigger, in request order.

A ``failed`` entry carries no ``trigger_id`` and no token — there is nothing to address, which is
what stops a failure from reading like a success. It carries ``retry`` instead: the endpoint that
creates *just this trigger*. Re-sending the agent-create call is never the right retry, because
that rotates the agent's worker token and invalidates any values.yaml already applied.
CreateAgentTriggerResult.title: CreateAgentTriggerResult

CreateAgentTriggerStatus.description:
What became of one requested trigger.

``unchanged`` is a success, not a no-op to worry about: it is what a retried create reports once
the trigger it asked for already exists and already matches.
CreateAgentTriggerStatus.title: CreateAgentTriggerStatus

name.title: Name

``ServerCreate`` + the control-plane-only fields: ABAC ``labels``, the catalog ``provider``,
and the ``probe_tool`` override.

allow.title: Allow

deny.description: Glob patterns of tool names to hide (wins over allow).
deny.title: Deny

name.title: Name

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client id for the client_credentials grant (not secret).
oauth_client_id.title: Oauth Client Id

oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth client secret as a ${env:VAR} or ${file:path} reference, resolved at connect time. Raw secrets are rejected so the registry never stores one.
oauth_client_secret.title: Oauth Client Secret

oauth_scopes.description: OAuth scopes to request; empty = server/registration default.
oauth_scopes.title: Oauth Scopes

oauth_token_url.description: Token endpoint for the client_credentials grant.
oauth_token_url.title: Oauth Token Url

Values may embed ${env:VAR} / ${file:path} secret references resolved at connect time — use those for credentials (e.g. 'Bearer ${env:API_TOKEN}'), because this field is stored in plaintext and returned by the admin read API.
static_headers.title: Static Headers

url.description: Endpoint URL for the upstream MCP server.
url.title: Url

CreateServerRequest.title: CreateServerRequest

CreateShadowWorkerTokenResponse.description:
The plaintext shadow worker token + hint, shown once — mirrors ``CreateWorkerTokenResponse``.
Defined locally rather than in ``agentops_rpc`` since nothing outside the control plane needs it
yet (no SDK/UI consumer in this change); the generated API client still picks it up from the
route's own type hints regardless of where the model lives.
CreateShadowWorkerTokenResponse.title: CreateShadowWorkerTokenResponse

CreateWorkflowDefinitionRequest.description: v1 creates definitions from a registered template only — no free-form graph writes.
CreateWorkflowDefinitionRequest.title: CreateWorkflowDefinitionRequest

CreatedOutpost.description: The create and rotate response: the Outpost, its one-time credential, and ready-to-run install values.
CreatedOutpost.title: CreatedOutpost

CredentialBinding.description:
An agent allowed to use a credential (push-delivery access policy).

``on_demand`` additionally lets a worker authenticated as this agent pull the
value outside of a run (e.g. a boot-time token); per-run push is unaffected.
CredentialBinding.title: CredentialBinding

CredentialBindingView.description:
A binding as the credential detail screen reads it: the wire model plus the bound agent's
display identity.

Kept here rather than widened onto ``CredentialBinding`` itself, which lives in ``agentops_rpc``
and is exported on the worker-facing surface. A label exists for an operator looking at a screen;
it is not part of the contract a worker speaks, and putting it there would oblige every future
consumer of that type to carry a field only this route populates.

``agent_name`` may be blank (an agent whose card carries no name); ``agent_id_slug`` never is.
CredentialBindingView.title: CredentialBindingView

CredentialKind.description:
What a credential *is*, so nobody outside the credential store has to parse its ``name``.

System-generated credentials used to encode their subject only in the name string (e.g.
``worker-token-<agent_id>``, ``webhook-token[-:]<target>``, …), which forced eight producers and
four *other* components to build or slice those strings by hand. The typed ``(kind, subject_id)``
pair is now authoritative: the credential vault resolves a system credential by kind + subject,
the ``name`` is kept only for its per-account uniqueness constraint, and no caller parses it.
CredentialKind.title: CredentialKind

CredentialMetadata.description:
Public, value-free view of a stored credential.

The encrypted value is never part of this model: it is write-only after
creation and only the Control Plane decrypt boundary ever sees plaintext.
CredentialMetadata.title: CredentialMetadata

DiscoveredOperation.description: One operation the document declares, as the operator's screens and the dial both see it.

summary.description: The document's own one-line summary, for the operation-picker table. Not stored on the server row.
summary.title: Summary

tool_name.description: The deterministic tool name this operation will become.
tool_name.title: Tool Name

DiscoveredOperation.title: DiscoveredOperation

DiscoveredTool.description:
One tool an upstream advertises, described for a human choosing a validation tool.

``safe_to_probe`` is whether the check may invoke it unattended, so the picker cannot offer a
tool the check would refuse to call. It is deliberately *wider* than what the automatic
selection picks: the heuristic also declines a tool that would answer without using the
credential, where an operator choosing that same tool by hand is making a judgement about their
own upstream and is honoured.
DiscoveredTool.title: DiscoveredTool

EnabledOperation.description:
One operation an operator turned on, and the tool it becomes.

Identity is ``(method, path)``, not ``operationId``: that field is optional in OpenAPI, which is
why the repo already ships ``assert_unique_operation_ids`` rather than trusting it.

method.description: Uppercase HTTP method, e.g. GET. Normalised on write.
method.title: Method

note.description: Operator-authored usage guidance, appended to the operation's description so it rides the tool.
note.title: Note

path.description: The operation's path template, exactly as the document declares it.
path.title: Path

tool_name.description: The deterministic tool name ingest assigned to this operation, computed over the full discovered inventory so de-selecting one operation can never rename another's tool. Kept here because it is short, and because it is what lets the dial reproduce the same tool for a (method, path) whatever else is enabled.
tool_name.title: Tool Name

EnabledOperation.title: EnabledOperation

EndpointWebhookAcceptedResponse.description:
Response for the standalone endpoint ingest route (``/webhooks/endpoint/{trigger_id}``).

A standalone endpoint accepts and captures the payload regardless of whether a target is
attached. ``routed`` is true when it dispatched to an agent/workflow; when no target is wired
yet it is false (the payload is captured for inspection but nothing runs).
EndpointWebhookAcceptedResponse.title: EndpointWebhookAcceptedResponse

EvalAdjustment.description:
One reason a score is off full marks, as the evaluator accounted for it.

`points` is signed and in the *evaluator's* scale (a grader reasoning in 100 points reports -6),
so the ledger reconciles against the arithmetic that was actually done; the rubric score itself
stays canonical 0..1 and is never recomputed from these. `kind` separates a deduction (additive)
from a ceiling (caps the score however well everything else went).
EvalAdjustment.title: EvalAdjustment

EvalCriterion.description:
One thing the evaluator checked, from its structured breakdown (`scores.detail_json`).

`score` is optional and `outcome` may stand alone: a qualitative check ("did it verify the claim
before asserting it") has a verdict and a reason but no meaningful number. Verdicts stored before
the explanation contract carry `name` + `score` only and read back with the rest empty.
EvalCriterion.title: EvalCriterion

EvalDetailResponse.description:
The graded run and every verdict on it. `title` is the run's own title, the same one the inbox
row carries, so the detail page names the run rather than echoing its id back at the reader.
EvalDetailResponse.title: EvalDetailResponse

EvalInboxRow.description:
One evaluated run in the evals inbox — every run carrying any quality verdict (LLM or human),
grouped by run. `title` is what to call the graded run (see :func:`agentops_rpc.run_title`), never
empty, so a row is scannable without falling back to the run id; `evaluated_at` is the most recent
verdict on the run. A run still has no single owning rule — it may be graded by several rules — so
the rule linkage lives per-verdict (`EvalVerdictChip.flow_id`), not on the row.
EvalInboxRow.title: EvalInboxRow

EvalSubject.description:
What one grading pass evaluates. ``RUN`` (default) is today's implicit single-run grading;
``RUN_PAIR`` grades a shadow-vs-production pair together (dual-deploy blinded pairwise judging).
EvalSubject.title: EvalSubject

EvalVerdictChip.description:
A compact verdict for the inbox row's chip strip: which evaluator, what score, which source.
`evaluator_id` is the score's `evaluator` (an evaluator's opaque agent_id) for LLM verdicts, or
the literal ``"human"`` pseudo-evaluator for human grades. `summary` is the verdict's one-line
rationale — the inbox renders only the score chip and ignores it; the agent eval-history shows it
as the per-evaluator reason. `flow_id`/`flow_name` name the eval rule that produced the verdict —
the same evaluator can grade one run under two rules, so this disambiguates the two chips (null
for human).
EvalVerdictChip.title: EvalVerdictChip

EvalVerdictDetail.description:
One review line on the eval-detail page: the evaluator's verdict with its full breakdown.
`method`/`criteria`/`adjustments`/`analysis` come from the LLM verdict's `scores.detail_json`
(empty for human grades, which carry only a numeric value + rationale) and are what the "Why this
score" block renders — how the number was computed, what was checked, what moved it, then the
prose. Every one is optional: an evaluator that fills none renders as it did before the
explanation contract. Human lines use the ``"human"``/"You" pseudo-evaluator. `flow_id`/`flow_name`
name the eval rule behind the verdict — one evaluator may produce two lines on the same run under
two rules, so the rule label tells them apart (null for human).
EvalVerdictDetail.title: EvalVerdictDetail

EvaluatorRosterRow.description:
A registered evaluator — an agent advertising the grader capability — with its recent
activity, for the Evaluators tab roster. ``evals_30d`` / ``avg_score`` aggregate the evaluator's
LLM verdicts in the window (its ``scores`` rows, keyed by ``evaluator == evaluator_id``); the id
is the opaque ``agent_id``, the same value flows store in ``evaluator_ids`` and the matcher stamps
as the score's ``evaluator``. ``last_active_at`` is the evaluator's most recent verdict, all-time.
``is_builtin`` is always False for now — built-in system evaluators are out of scope (PRD).
Which flows an evaluator sits on is derived on the client from the flow list, not carried here.
EvaluatorRosterRow.title: EvaluatorRosterRow

ExtremeRun.description:
One end of a rubric's range for an agent: the run, what it scored, and enough to link to it.

`score` is the run's mean on that rubric — a panel of evaluators measuring one rubric on one run
is a mean worth taking — so a run appears at most once per rubric rather than once per verdict.
ExtremeRun.title: ExtremeRun

FindingStatus.description: A finding's lifecycle. A ``FIXED``/``DISMISSED`` finding seen again reopens as ``OPEN``.
FindingStatus.title: FindingStatus

FleetOverviewRequest.description:
Window and optional agent facet for the fleet-wide run aggregate.

``agent_ids`` absent means account-wide; an empty list means an empty selection, which returns
zeros rather than everything. There is deliberately no ``include_archived``: this aggregates
``runs``, which carries no archival flag (that lives on the agent record, owned elsewhere), so
the account-wide totals include the runs of archived agents. A facet posted from an
archived-excluding agent list narrows them out again.
FleetOverviewRequest.title: FleetOverviewRequest

FleetOverviewResponse.description:
Fleet-wide run totals, the daily activity grid, model mix and the two agent leaderboards.

``buckets`` is dense: one entry per calendar day of the window, zero-filled, ending today, so a
consumer can render a grid column per element without gap handling. ``model_mix`` is bounded:
the tail beyond the largest few models is folded into a single ``(other)`` entry, so the slices
still sum to the fleet totals. Quotients (``cost_per_run``, ``avg_latency_ms``) are ``None``,
never ``0``, when their denominator is empty.
FleetOverviewResponse.title: FleetOverviewResponse

FleetStatusRequest.description:
Optional agent facet for the fleet-wide live status rollup.

Deliberately carries no ``window_days``: this reports state right now (who is online, how many
replicas are live, what is queued), not flow over a period. ``agent_ids`` absent means every
agent the caller may read; an empty list means an empty selection and returns zeros.
FleetStatusRequest.title: FleetStatusRequest

FleetStatusResponse.description:
The fleet's live state: composition, capacity, backlog, reachability and version mix.

**Composition** is exhaustive over the agents in scope — ``draft + online + offline_recent +
offline_long`` equals their count. ``draft`` is "never reported in" (no heartbeat ever), and
merges the mid-deploy and deploy-failed refinements the agents list shows separately.

**Capacity** (``live_replicas``, ``busy_replicas``) and **version mix** are narrowed to the
primary dual-deploy arm and to heartbeat-fresh replicas, so they will not equal the sum of the
agents list's ``instances_total`` on the same screen. ``busy_replicas`` counts only fresh
replicas too, so ``active_runs`` can legitimately exceed it: a dead pod can still own a claimed
run.

**Reachability** is over heartbeat-online agents only — an offline agent is not "unreachable",
it is offline — and it is agent-level and **arm-blind**: the underlying presence read returns the
freshest channel sighting across every replica, primary or shadow. A shadow-only-live agent can
therefore read reachable beside 0 live primary replicas.

The three id lists are the actionable call-outs, so each count can be rendered as chips rather
than a bare number: agents that went offline within the last hour, heartbeat-online agents with
no live primary replica, and the online-but-unreachable ones (``unreachable_agents ==
len(unreachable_agent_ids)`` by construction).
FleetStatusResponse.title: FleetStatusResponse

GatewayOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
GatewayOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: GatewayOnboardingCompletionResponse

GatewayProvisionOutcome.description:
What :meth:`ModelProvisioningPort.provision_account` did — the transport-agnostic outcome the
port returns (the decision ``model`` now makes internally, folded in from the caller's old
``is_configured`` / ``uses_hosted_proxy`` pre-flight gates), so a consumer reacts to it instead of
reading gateway config.

Lives in the kernel, not in the published ``agentops_rpc``: it is an internal control↔model
contract value, never part of the worker-facing wire surface. On the HTTP transport it rides
inside ``model``'s own response schema (consumed via the generated ``agentops_model_client``); the
in-process implementation returns it directly.
GatewayProvisionOutcome.title: GatewayProvisionOutcome

GatewayProvisionResult.description:
Response of the provision endpoint — the wire form of the port's
:class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.GatewayProvisionOutcome`. This is the
schema the generated ``agentops_model_client`` re-derives; the transport-agnostic enum it wraps
lives in the kernel so the in-process path never depends on the generated client.
GatewayProvisionResult.title: GatewayProvisionResult

GoldenAuthoringStatus.description:
Lifecycle of the `scenario-author` worker run that fills in a scenario's first version, once
one has been kicked off for it — `authoring_run_id`/`authoring_status` are both unset until then.
GoldenAuthoringStatus.title: GoldenAuthoringStatus

GoldenRunFailureKind.description:
Which phase of the run pipeline failed, normally when `status` is `failed`/`blocked`.

`JUDGE` is the one member also set on a `completed` run: the scenario execution itself succeeded,
but the run was never graded (no judge could be dispatched for it), so the run stays `completed`
and this marks the grade as missing rather than the run as failed. Everywhere else, a kind is only
ever set alongside a failed/blocked status.
GoldenRunFailureKind.title: GoldenRunFailureKind

GoldenRunsAccess.description:
Whether a golden scenario run can actually be handed this connection's credential.

Three states rather than a boolean because "no" has two causes an operator resolves
differently: a credential nobody has designated (fixable in one click) and a provider whose
fields are not mapped to worker env vars at all (only a code change adds it). Collapsing them
sends someone to press a button that cannot help.
GoldenRunsAccess.title: GoldenRunsAccess

GoldenValidationLevel.description:
How rigorously a version's content has been vetted before being trusted for grading — shared
between the version's own record and the snapshot a run takes of it at execution time.
GoldenValidationLevel.title: GoldenValidationLevel

deny.description: Group-level deny globs, layered on top of server rules; deny wins.

GroupPatch.description: Partial update for a group; unset fields are left unchanged.
GroupPatch.title: GroupPatch
