GuardRailsBuffer.description: Percent overhead a workload is left to absorb further load increases with.
GuardRailsBuffer.title: GuardRailsBuffer

GuardRailsConstraints.description:
Relative right-sizing step limits. Units are not documented anywhere on Komodor's side —
not assumed to be percent here either.
GuardRailsConstraints.title: GuardRailsConstraints

GuardrailApprovalResponse.description:
One held call, as the person deciding it sees it.

``arguments`` is what makes the decision possible — the call's own arguments, the one place this
feature stores them. Reading them needs ``guardrail.read`` and answering needs ``guardrail.approve``;
an approval request that named only the tool would be a rubber stamp.

``is_expired`` is derived rather than stored: a row does not change when a clock passes it, and an
expired approval can no longer be answered or spent.
GuardrailApprovalResponse.title: GuardrailApprovalResponse

GuardrailGate.description:
Where a guardrail stands: the point traffic passes through and can be stopped at.

Three are expressible. The remaining gates from the PRD — a trigger payload, a model response —
arrive with the phase that can inspect them.

``TOOL_RESPONSE`` is the first one on the **inbound** leg, and it exists because the other two cannot
reach the risk it covers: a secret, a customer record or an injected instruction arriving *back* from
a tool is content no outbound gate ever sees. What it stops is the content entering the agent's
context, not the call — the call has already run by the time this gate is asked, which is a property
of where it stands and not a limitation to work around (see :func:`gate_outcome_problem`).
GuardrailGate.title: GuardrailGate

GuardrailOutcome.description:
What a boundary does about a covered call.

It lives in the contract rather than inside governance because the boundary *acts* on it: the seam
has to tell a refusal from an observation, and a string literal at that branch is the one place
this vocabulary could silently fork. Governance still owns which outcome a given call gets.

Every value names the call's fate, and nothing else — the disposition axis, which is what lets the
values be ordered by severity at all. Recording is not one of them: every decision is audited
whatever the outcome, so a value meaning "record it" would name a side effect the others share and
could not be ranked against them.
GuardrailOutcome.title: GuardrailOutcome

IdentityContext.description: The resolved identity for a session: who they are, how they signed in, and where.
IdentityContext.title: IdentityContext

ImpersonationContext.description:
Set only while a session is acting under a system-admin impersonation or cross-account view.

Its presence *is* the "you are impersonating" signal; it names the originating admin so the UI
can show a banner with an Exit affordance and audit can attribute the real actor (the ``user``/
``account``/``principal`` on the enclosing :class:`IdentityContext` describe the TARGET).
ImpersonationContext.title: ImpersonationContext

ImpersonationMode.description:
How a system-admin session is acting. Stored in the signed cookie's ``act_as`` claim and
surfaced on :class:`ImpersonationContext`.
ImpersonationMode.title: ImpersonationMode

ImportScenarioResponse.description:
The result of importing an uploaded scenario bundle: the created scenario and its first
version, plus the full intake report (see `controlplane.components.optimize.goldens.intake`) —
a 201 can still carry warnings worth surfacing even though nothing hard-blocked.
ImportScenarioResponse.title: ImportScenarioResponse

IncidentDetailResponse.description:
``GET /incidents/{id}`` response — the incident detail plus its aggregate investigation stats
(duration/tokens/cost/errors), flattened onto the same object the UI's ``PlatformIncidentDetail``
already expects (additive field, so it's wire-compatible before the UI's stats card ships).
IncidentDetailResponse.title: IncidentDetailResponse

pct_automated.description: Percentage (0-100) of RESOLVED incidents whose resolution_source is 'automated'.

avg_run_duration_seconds.description: Mean wall-clock duration of the window's runs; null when no run recorded both ends.
avg_run_duration_seconds.title: Avg Run Duration Seconds

IncidentsOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
IncidentsOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: IncidentsOnboardingCompletionResponse

IntegrationConnectionDetail.description: Connection metadata. Secret values are never returned.
IntegrationConnectionDetail.title: IntegrationConnectionDetail

IntegrationsOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
IntegrationsOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: IntegrationsOnboardingCompletionResponse

InternalAccountResponse.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.AccountRef` — the scoped
account's identity fields. No request body / ``account_id`` field: the account read is always the
header account the wall authenticated (the IDOR guard).
InternalAccountResponse.title: InternalAccountResponse

InternalAgentIdsRequest.description:
Agent-id batch request. ``Internal``-prefixed like every schema in this slice — a plain
``AgentIdsRequest`` also exists in control's internal API, and sharing the name (and OpenAPI
title) makes the generated clients drop one side's endpoints.
InternalAgentIdsRequest.title: InternalAgentIdsRequest

InternalAgentMetric.description: Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.AgentRunMetrics`, keyed by agent.
InternalAgentMetric.title: InternalAgentMetric

InternalAgentRunFacts.description: Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.AgentRunFacts`, keyed by agent.
InternalAgentRunFacts.title: InternalAgentRunFacts

InternalAgentWindowRequest.description:
Agent-id batch plus the window it is measured over.

Separate from ``InternalAgentIdsRequest`` rather than widening it: that model is shared by three
endpoints with no window of their own, so adding the field would change their schemas too. The
bounds match the public fleet request: this is the surface the agents-list window parameter
reaches, so leaving it unbounded here would bound only half the path.
InternalAgentWindowRequest.title: InternalAgentWindowRequest

InternalCancelRunRequest.description:
Body for the run-cancel endpoint — the wire form of ``cancel``'s ``reason`` kwarg. The account
is the authenticated identity's (never a body field) and the actor is rebuilt server-side, like
RUN_DISPATCH: runtime owns run audit and never trusts a caller-sent actor.
InternalCancelRunRequest.title: InternalCancelRunRequest

InternalCatalogDeployResponse.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.CatalogDeployResult` — the
one field the Slack connect hook needs, so the caller never depends on ``HostedAgentResponse``.
``Internal``-prefixed so it never collides with another slice's schema.
InternalCatalogDeployResponse.title: InternalCatalogDeployResponse

InternalChannelPresence.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.ChannelPresence`, keyed by
the agent it belongs to (the port returns a ``{agent_id -> presence}`` map the twin rebuilds).
InternalChannelPresence.title: InternalChannelPresence

InternalChannelSpecTrigger.description:
One ``slack_channel`` trigger row control already read (``source_id``, ``config_json``,
``input_json``, ``is_enabled``) — the wire form of the dicts ``sync_agent`` reconciles into
``channel_routes``. The JSON columns are free-form objects; ``source_id`` scopes the derived route
back to its declaration.
InternalChannelSpecTrigger.title: InternalChannelSpecTrigger

InternalConnectedProvidersResponse.description:
The set of actively-connected integration providers for the scoped account. A ``list`` on the
wire (JSON has no set); the twin rebuilds the ``set`` the in-process port returns.
InternalConnectedProvidersResponse.title: InternalConnectedProvidersResponse

InternalConnection.description:
The internal wire form of ``IntegrationConnection`` — the same safe fields (no secret columns),
but its own model so the generated component client stays clean. It cannot reuse the shared
``agentops_rpc.IntegrationConnection`` here: that model's ``metadata`` carries ``title=IntegrationMetadata``,
a free-form ``dict[str, Any]`` title also worn by the ``IntegrationConnectionDetail`` subclass in this
same OpenAPI slice, so the generator drops the duplicated model and leaves a dangling import in the
generated ``IntegrationConnection.from_dict``. This model gives ``metadata`` a slice-unique title so it
generates as a usable additional-properties map; the twin rebuilds the shared DTO from it.
InternalConnection.title: InternalConnection

InternalCreateCredentialRequest.description:
Body for the credential-create endpoint — the wire form of ``create_credential``'s kwargs a
cross-component caller passes, minus the backend (security seals) and the account (forced from the
token). ``kind`` is typed as the enum so an unknown value fails as a clean 422 here, not a 500.
InternalCreateCredentialRequest.title: InternalCreateCredentialRequest

InternalCreateRunRequest.description:
Body for the run-dispatch endpoint — the wire form of the ``create_run`` /
``create_run_with_dedup`` kwargs a cross-component caller passes. Only the fields consumers
actually use are carried; the twin raises on any other kwarg rather than silently dropping it, so a
new caller kwarg is a compile-time-visible schema change, not a lost value.
InternalCreateRunRequest.title: InternalCreateRunRequest

InternalCreateRunResponse.description:
Response of the run-dispatch endpoint: the created (or idempotency-matched) run and whether it
was newly created. ``created`` is False on an idempotency conflict — the twin's
``create_run_with_dedup`` returns it; ``create_run`` discards it.
InternalCreateRunResponse.title: InternalCreateRunResponse

InternalCredentialIdByNameRequest.description:
Body for the id-by-name lookup. ``kind``/``owner`` scope it to a system credential of that
kind/owner (see ``credentials.service.get_credential_id_by_name``), matching
``InternalResolveCredentialByNameRequest``'s convention above.
InternalCredentialIdByNameRequest.title: InternalCredentialIdByNameRequest

InternalCredentialSubjectsResponse.description:
``{subject_id -> credential_id}`` for every credential of ``kind`` — see
``credentials.service.list_credential_subjects``. ``title`` gives the map a specific generated-model
name, matching ``InternalResolvedSecretsResponse.secrets`` / ``InternalUpdateCredentialMetadataRequest
.labels`` above.
InternalCredentialSubjectsResponse.title: InternalCredentialSubjectsResponse

InternalDeleteReplicasRequest.description: Body for the teardown half — clear every ``worker_instances`` row for one agent (account-scoped).
InternalDeleteReplicasRequest.title: InternalDeleteReplicasRequest

InternalDeleteReplicasResponse.description: Acknowledgement of the teardown write. Idempotent: ``ok`` is True whether or not any row existed.
InternalDeleteReplicasResponse.title: InternalDeleteReplicasResponse

InternalEnsureAgentDefaultRoleResponse.description:
The built-in role slug granted (``agent``), or ``None`` when nothing was written — the principal
already held a role assignment, or the built-in role is not seeded (best-effort). ``Internal``-prefixed
so it never collides with another slice's OpenAPI schema.
InternalEnsureAgentDefaultRoleResponse.title: InternalEnsureAgentDefaultRoleResponse

InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalRequest.description:
Body for the agent-principal provisioning write. The account is the authenticated service
identity's (``X-AgentOps-Account-Id``), never a body field; ``agent_id`` is the path parameter.
``now`` is the caller's heartbeat timestamp (carried so the minted principal's timestamps match
the beat, not the round-trip), mirroring ``register_worker_replica``. Kept a ``str`` for wire
compatibility (it flows straight into the ISO-text ``created_at`` / ``updated_at`` columns), but
validated as ISO-8601 so a malformed value from a misconfigured caller fails as a clean 422 here
rather than an opaque Postgres error downstream.
InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalRequest.title: InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalRequest

InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalResponse.description:
The agent's principal id — existing or freshly minted. Never ``None`` over the wall: the
account is always resolved from the token here (``_scoped_account_id`` rejects an absent scope),
so the in-process port's ``None`` (unknown-account skip) can't occur on this path.
InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalResponse.title: InternalEnsureAgentPrincipalResponse

InternalGetConnectionResponse.description:
``connection=None`` when no (account-scoped) connection matches — the caller degrades exactly as
the in-process port's ``None`` return does.
InternalGetConnectionResponse.title: InternalGetConnectionResponse

InternalGetCredentialResponse.description:
``credential=None`` when no (account-scoped) credential matches — the caller degrades exactly as
the in-process port's ``None`` return does.
InternalGetCredentialResponse.title: InternalGetCredentialResponse

InternalGoldenCredentialledProvidersRequ.description: The providers to test. Only the *providers* are a body field — the account is never one.
InternalGoldenCredentialledProvidersRequ.title: InternalGoldenCredentialledProvidersRequest

InternalGuardrailDecisionModel.description:
The rule covering a call: its id, the name a refusal shows an operator, and the outcome to act on.
Mirrors :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.GuardrailDecision`.
InternalGuardrailDecisionModel.title: InternalGuardrailDecisionModel

InternalGuardrailEvaluateResponse.description:
``decision`` is ``None`` when no guardrail covers the call.

An envelope with a nullable field rather than a bare 200/204 pair, because "nothing covered this
call" means *let it through* — and a generated client hands back ``None`` for more than one kind of
non-answer. Making the allow explicit in a 200 body keeps a failed request from being read as
permission: anything that is not a 200 raises on the client side, and the boundary's own error path
refuses the call.
InternalGuardrailEvaluateResponse.title: InternalGuardrailEvaluateResponse

InternalGuardrailHoldResponse.description:
How a ``hold`` resolved: the approval the call concerns, and whether it is already granted.
Mirrors :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.GuardrailHold`.
InternalGuardrailHoldResponse.title: InternalGuardrailHoldResponse

InternalGuardrailToolResponseRequest.description:
One tool result to decide on, carrying the actor because the same call also records the decision.

``texts`` are the response's content blocks already flattened by the boundary — the gate needs the
content to decide and nothing here writes it down, which is why it rides in a POST body rather than a
query string that would reach access logs.
InternalGuardrailToolResponseRequest.title: InternalGuardrailToolResponseRequest

InternalInstallResponse.description: The install a principal authenticates as, or nulls for every other caller.
InternalInstallResponse.title: InternalInstallResponse

InternalInstallationTokenResponse.description:
The minted GitHub App installation token blob (``access_token``, ``expires_at``, ``permissions``,
…). A slice-unique title on the free-form map, like the payload models above.
InternalInstallationTokenResponse.title: InternalInstallationTokenResponse

InternalInvalidateRegistrationResponse.description: Acknowledgement of the digest-clear write. Idempotent: ``ok`` is True whether or not a row matched.
InternalInvalidateRegistrationResponse.title: InternalInvalidateRegistrationResponse

InternalKomodorAccountLinkResponse.description:
The scoped account's Komodor account link. No request body / ``account_id`` field: the read is
always the header account the wall authenticated (the IDOR guard).
InternalKomodorAccountLinkResponse.title: InternalKomodorAccountLinkResponse

InternalListCredentialsResponse.description:
Shared response shape for the plain account list and the per-agent list below — a list rather
than the operator-facing paginated envelope, since neither in-scope caller (``gateway``'s internal-MCP
inspection tools) pages this.
InternalListCredentialsResponse.title: InternalListCredentialsResponse

InternalManagedSecretRequest.description:
Body for the managed-secret write. ``payload`` is the provider secret blob to seal (a slice-unique
title so it generates as a usable additional-properties map, like ``InternalConnection.metadata``).
InternalManagedSecretRequest.title: InternalManagedSecretRequest

InternalOwnersResponse.description:
Owners keyed by resource id. A resource with no claim is simply absent — and a present entry is a
statement about provenance, never that the resource still exists.
InternalOwnersResponse.title: InternalOwnersResponse

InternalParsedAlert.description:
Wire form of a gateway-parsed :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.ParsedAlert`.
The gateway extracts structured alerts from provider payloads (multi-alert AlertManager envelopes and
the firing/resolved lifecycle) using the *trigger's* alert config, which ``incidents`` does not own and
so cannot re-derive from ``raw_body`` alone — the parsed list therefore crosses the wall explicitly.
``status`` is the ``AlertStatus`` string value (``firing``/``resolved``).
InternalParsedAlert.title: InternalParsedAlert

InternalPatchRunTitleRequest.description:
Body for the output-title patch — the wire form of ``patch_title``'s kwargs. The account is the
authenticated identity's, never a body field.
InternalPatchRunTitleRequest.title: InternalPatchRunTitleRequest

InternalPatchRunTitleResponse.description:
Acknowledgement of the patch write. Idempotent: ``ok`` is True whether or not the run existed in
this account (the underlying UPDATE is a no-op WHERE-match miss, not an error).
InternalPatchRunTitleResponse.title: InternalPatchRunTitleResponse

InternalPipelineAccountResponse.description:
The pipeline's owning account, or ``None`` when no such pipeline exists (the not-found signal the
caller renders as an absent target).
InternalPipelineAccountResponse.title: InternalPipelineAccountResponse

InternalPipelineExistsResponse.description:
Whether the pipeline exists within the authenticated account. Names are ``Internal``-prefixed so
they never collide with another slice's schema.
InternalPipelineExistsResponse.title: InternalPipelineExistsResponse

InternalQueueCount.description: Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.RunQueueCount`, keyed by agent.
InternalQueueCount.title: InternalQueueCount

InternalRawGrantsResponse.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.authz.ports.RawGrants` — one principal's grant
snapshot, read under a single connection so the returned view is consistent, exactly as the
in-process reader guarantees. ``title`` gives the two map/attr fields specific generated-model
names so they never collide with another slice's inline map (the openapi-python-client
duplicate-name failure mode).
InternalRawGrantsResponse.title: InternalRawGrantsResponse

InternalRawRoleMemberGrant.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.authz.ports.RawRoleMemberGrant`. ``resource_selector``
is a JSON string (or ``None``), same as :class:`InternalRawSubjectGrant`.
InternalRawRoleMemberGrant.title: InternalRawRoleMemberGrant

InternalRawSubjectGrant.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.authz.ports.RawSubjectGrant`. ``resource_selector``
is carried as a JSON **string** (or ``None``) — the raw-JSON-over-a-text-transport shape the port
already documents; ``resolve._table_grants`` runs it through ``from_json``, which accepts either a
string or a dict, so the grant-building logic is byte-for-byte identical to the in-process read.
InternalRawSubjectGrant.title: InternalRawSubjectGrant

InternalReadSecretPayloadRequest.description: Body (not a path/query) so the credential id never lands in an access log or URL.
InternalReadSecretPayloadRequest.title: InternalReadSecretPayloadRequest

InternalRecordAuthzCheckRequest.description:
Facts for one point-check decision — the arguments of :meth:`DecisionSink.record_check`, minus
``flags`` (the server uses its own). ``detail`` is the engine's neutral bag (provider, mode,
would-decision, pdp-failed, latency, surface); ``title`` keeps its generated map name unique.
InternalRecordAuthzCheckRequest.title: InternalRecordAuthzCheckRequest

InternalRecordAuthzFilterRequest.description:
Facts for one list-filter resolution — the arguments of :meth:`DecisionSink.record_filter`,
minus ``flags``. Same ``detail`` bag convention as :class:`InternalRecordAuthzCheckRequest`.
InternalRecordAuthzFilterRequest.title: InternalRecordAuthzFilterRequest

InternalRecordConnectionTestRequest.description:
Body for the connection-test audit record. ``record_audit`` is the boolean twin of the caller's
``audit_actor`` (the actor object never crosses the wire — it encodes request identity a callee can't
trust from a caller); the route rebuilds the actor server-side from the authenticated identity.
InternalRecordConnectionTestRequest.title: InternalRecordConnectionTestRequest

InternalRefreshPresenceRequest.description:
Body for the presence fast-path — the wire form of ``refresh_presence``'s kwargs. The account is
the authenticated identity's, never a body field. ``manifest_hash`` is the caller's evidence that
nothing changed (``None`` asks the weaker "is this replica registered at all" question).
InternalRefreshPresenceRequest.title: InternalRefreshPresenceRequest

InternalRefreshPresenceResponse.description:
``matched`` is True when a registered replica's heartbeat was bumped; False means the caller must
fall through to a full ``register_replica``.
InternalRefreshPresenceResponse.title: InternalRefreshPresenceResponse

InternalRegisterReplicaRequest.description:
Body for the worker-registration write — the wire form of ``register_replica``'s kwargs. The
account is the authenticated identity's, never a body field. ``now`` is the caller's heartbeat
timestamp (carried so the replica's ``last_heartbeat_at`` matches the beat, not the round-trip).
InternalRegisterReplicaRequest.title: InternalRegisterReplicaRequest

InternalRegisterReplicaResponse.description:
``(generation, newly_minted)`` — the caller writes its generation-ledger row keyed on the
returned ``generation``; ``newly_minted`` is True only when a new generation was minted.
InternalRegisterReplicaResponse.title: InternalRegisterReplicaResponse

InternalReleaseResponse.description:
Whether there was a claim to drop. Not an error when there was not — the resync releases on a 404
and may race another release.
InternalReleaseResponse.title: InternalReleaseResponse

InternalReplaceCredentialValueRequest.description:
Body for the credential value-rotation endpoint — ``replace_value``'s kwargs minus the backend and
account. ``credential_id`` is the path parameter; ``reassert_kind`` re-stamps a system credential's
typed identity as part of the rotation (see ``credentials.service.replace_value``).
InternalReplaceCredentialValueRequest.title: InternalReplaceCredentialValueRequest

InternalResolveCredentialByNameRequest.description:
``kind``/``owner`` scope the lookup to a system credential of that kind/owner (see
``credentials.service.resolve_value_by_name``), so a user credential sharing the name can't shadow
a system one. ``kind`` is typed as the enum so an unknown value fails as a clean 422.
InternalResolveCredentialByNameRequest.title: InternalResolveCredentialByNameRequest

InternalResolveCredentialBySubjectReques.description:
Resolve the active ``(kind, subject_id)`` system credential (see
``credentials.service.resolve_value_by_subject``).
InternalResolveCredentialBySubjectReques.title: InternalResolveCredentialBySubjectRequest

InternalResolveGrantsRequest.description:
The ``(principal_id, account_id)`` a split deployable is authorizing — the arguments of the
in-process :meth:`SqlGrantReader.read`. The account is a body field, not the token scope: the
caller authenticates globally and names the account it is resolving grants for.
InternalResolveGrantsRequest.title: InternalResolveGrantsRequest

InternalResolveIdentityRequest.description:
The credential a split deployable's request presented, forwarded for resolution. ``headers`` are
the forwardable credential + service headers verbatim (``Authorization`` / ``Cookie`` / ``X-Agent-Id``
/ the ``X-AgentOps-Service-*`` set) — carried as a body field, NOT real request headers, so
``security``'s own wall (which authenticates the calling deployable's *global* service token) never
tries to interpret them. ``expected_servers`` are the calling deployable's accepted service
audiences — the ``svc:<component>`` names it composes — so a forwarded account-scoped service token
verifies against *its* audiences, not ``security``'s. It is a set (not the deployable's single
``SERVICE_NAME``) because a token is addressed to the component it calls, which differs from the
deployable name when a deployable hosts a component under another name or bundles several.

The map field is ``credential_headers`` (not ``headers``) so its generated wire model has a unique
name — a bare ``headers`` collides with the inline ``Headers`` model another route's schema
generates, churning that slice's client (the openapi-python-client duplicate-name failure mode).
The originating actor is not a separate field — it rides in ``credential_headers`` as
``X-AgentOps-Actor``, which ``_authenticate_service`` reads on resolution.
InternalResolveIdentityRequest.title: InternalResolveIdentityRequest

InternalResolveIdentityResponse.description:
The resolution outcome. ``outcome=RESOLVED`` carries the reconstructed :class:`IdentityContext`
(the same shape ``/auth/me`` serves — reused, not re-declared, so the wire form can never drift from
the real identity) plus the worker request-state a worker mechanism sets (``agent_id`` /
``is_dev_worker``, both ``None`` otherwise); ``SHORT_CIRCUIT`` carries the terminal ``status_code`` +
``detail`` (e.g. a 503) the far wall rebuilds; ``NONE`` means no credential resolved → challenge.
InternalResolveIdentityResponse.title: InternalResolveIdentityResponse

InternalResolveOnDemandSecretsRequest.description:
``worker_id`` is the replica asking, and it keys the tool credential this resolve mints so a
re-pull overwrites its own record instead of adding one. Nullable because the body itself is
optional (see the handler), so the wire has a shape for a caller with no replica to name: it
resolves the agent's credentials and is issued no tool credential, one bound to no replica being
attributable to no holder and revocable through no record.
InternalResolveOnDemandSecretsRequest.title: InternalResolveOnDemandSecretsRequest

InternalResolvedSecretResponse.description:
One credential's plaintext, base64-encoded (a secret is arbitrary bytes, not guaranteed UTF-8).
``value_b64`` is ``None`` when no active credential matches the (account-scoped) lookup or no master
key is configured — the caller degrades exactly as it did when the pre-port decrypt returned None.
InternalResolvedSecretResponse.title: InternalResolvedSecretResponse

InternalResolvedSecretsResponse.description:
``{name -> plaintext}`` for the agent. The ``title`` gives the map a specific generated-model name
(rather than a bare ``Secrets`` that could collide with another slice's inline map in the composed
client and silently drop an endpoint — the openapi-python-client title-collision failure mode).
InternalResolvedSecretsResponse.title: InternalResolvedSecretsResponse

InternalReviewWebhookSinkRequest.description:
Wire form of the ``gateway``→``code_review`` webhook hand-off. ``raw_body_b64`` is the raw
endpoint body base64-encoded so arbitrary (possibly non-JSON, non-UTF-8) webhook bytes cross the
wall losslessly — the sink itself parses it and owns the exact HTTP-400 message, so the gateway
still never reads it. ``headers`` carries the inbound request headers the review handler inspects
(e.g. the GitHub event type). Names are ``Internal``-prefixed so they never collide with another
slice's schema.
InternalReviewWebhookSinkRequest.title: InternalReviewWebhookSinkRequest

InternalReviewWebhookSinkResponse.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.ReviewWebhookDispatch`.
``results`` is one arbitrary JSON object per matched workflow (already merged with its
``workflow_id``), passed through unchanged — the shape the gateway's response builder expects.
InternalReviewWebhookSinkResponse.title: InternalReviewWebhookSinkResponse

InternalRunStats.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.RunStatsRow`. The two
timestamps ride as ``datetime`` so the generated client parses them back to aware ``datetime``
objects the twin returns unchanged.
InternalRunStats.title: InternalRunStats

InternalSecretPayloadResponse.description:
The decrypted secret payload. Sensitive by construction — returned only over the service-auth
wall to another first-party deployable (decision B(i): ``read_secret_payload`` stays a port).
InternalSecretPayloadResponse.title: InternalSecretPayloadResponse

InternalSetAgentRolesRequest.description:
Replace an agent's unscoped role assignments. ``account_id`` is deliberately absent — the
account is the token's (the IDOR guard), like every other write on this router.

``record_audit`` rather than an actor object, matching the credential write/binding endpoints:
attribution encodes impersonation and system-admin context that a caller must not be able to
assert over the wall, so the far side rebuilds it from the authenticated request and this flag
only says whether the assignment should write its ``ROLE_ASSIGN`` row at all.
InternalSetAgentRolesRequest.title: InternalSetAgentRolesRequest

InternalSetAgentRolesResponse.description: The agent's effective unscoped role ids after the diff.
InternalSetAgentRolesResponse.title: InternalSetAgentRolesResponse

InternalSubscribeAgentRequest.description:
Subscribe one agent to one sink, idempotently. ``account_id`` is deliberately absent — the
account is the token's (the IDOR guard), and the sink is looked up under it.

``record_audit`` rather than an actor object, matching the credential and role endpoints:
attribution encodes impersonation and system-admin context a caller must not be able to assert
over the wall, so this flag only says whether the ``NOTIFICATION_SINK_SUBSCRIBE`` row should be
written at all and the far side supplies the actor itself. Note what that means and does not: the
row's actor is the *authenticated caller of this route*, which over the wall is the calling
deployable's service principal rather than the operator who started it. Same trade the credential
and role surfaces already make — the alternative is trusting a caller's claim about who it is
acting for. A re-subscribe that changes nothing writes no row either way.

Deliberately **not** ``extra="forbid"``, like its siblings on the other internal routers. Pydantic
drops an unknown field, so a caller-named ``account_id`` cannot influence anything here — and
forbidding extras instead would turn a rolling upgrade, where a newer deployable sends a field an
older pod has not learned yet, into a 422 rather than a tolerated no-op.
InternalSubscribeAgentRequest.title: InternalSubscribeAgentRequest

InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesRequest.description:
Body for the channel-spec-route materialisation — the wire form of ``sync_agent``'s kwargs. The
account is the authenticated identity's, never a body field. ``now`` is the caller's heartbeat
timestamp (carried so a materialised route's ``created_at`` / ``updated_at`` matches the beat).
InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesRequest.title: InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesRequest

InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesResponse.description: Acknowledgement of the reconcile write. Idempotent: ``ok`` is True whether or not any route changed.
InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesResponse.title: InternalSyncChannelSpecRoutesResponse

InternalToolCall.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.ToolCallRow`.

``arguments`` crosses the wall because a guardrail can condition on it; it stays inside the
service-auth boundary and is never echoed to a caller — a tool argument can carry a credential.
InternalToolCall.title: InternalToolCall

InternalToolCallRequest.description:
Wire form of a ``GATEWAY_TOOL_CALL.call_tool``: the catalog tool name and its arguments. The
account is taken from the service-auth scope, never carried here.
InternalToolCallRequest.title: InternalToolCallRequest

InternalToolCallResponse.description:
The MCP ``CallToolResult`` as a json object (an ``isError`` result rides here as a normal 200 —
only a resolve/transport failure surfaces as a non-200).
InternalToolCallResponse.title: InternalToolCallResponse

InternalUpdateCredentialMetadataRequest.description:
Body for the metadata-patch endpoint — the wire form of ``update_metadata``'s kwargs the one
caller (``model``) passes: a wholesale labels replacement plus the audit ``actor`` string. Narrower
than ``UpdateCredentialMetadataRequest`` (the operator-facing PATCH), which also carries
description/owner/status — not needed here and left off until a caller needs them (issue #3415).
InternalUpdateCredentialMetadataRequest.title: InternalUpdateCredentialMetadataRequest

InternalUpdateStatusRequest.description:
Body for the status flip. Every live caller passes a synthetic ``INTERNAL`` audit actor (a
non-PII ``actor_type``/``actor_label`` pair), so only its ``actor_label`` rides the wire and the
route rebuilds it via ``internal_audit_actor_ref`` — an unset label means no audit row.
InternalUpdateStatusRequest.title: InternalUpdateStatusRequest

InternalWebhookSinkRequest.description:
Wire form of the ``gateway``→``incidents`` webhook hand-off. ``raw_body_b64`` is the raw endpoint
body base64-encoded so arbitrary (possibly non-JSON, non-UTF-8) webhook bytes cross the wall
losslessly — the sink itself parses it and owns the exact HTTP-400 message, so the gateway still
never reads it. ``alerts`` carries the gateway's pre-parsed alerts when the trigger is alert-typed
(absent otherwise, so the sink parses ``raw_body`` itself). Names are ``Internal``-prefixed so they
never collide with another slice's schema.
InternalWebhookSinkRequest.title: InternalWebhookSinkRequest

InternalWebhookSinkResponse.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.IncidentWebhookDispatch`.
``results`` is one arbitrary JSON object per matched pipeline (already merged with its
``pipeline_id``), passed through unchanged — the shape the gateway's response builder expects.
InternalWebhookSinkResponse.title: InternalWebhookSinkResponse

InternalWorkerInstance.description:
Wire form of :class:`~agentops_shared.infra.component_contract.ports.WorkerInstanceRow` (its own
columns only — ``agent_id`` is the enclosing item's map key, never repeated per replica).
InternalWorkerInstance.title: InternalWorkerInstance

InternalWorkerTokenStatusRequest.title: InternalWorkerTokenStatusRequest

InternalWorkerTokenStatusResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the twin rebuilds
the ``{agent_id -> WorkerTokenStatus}`` dict the port returns.
InternalWorkerTokenStatusResponse.title: InternalWorkerTokenStatusResponse

JudgedCriterionModel.description:
One predicate a **model** decides: a stated policy, and the model that judges it.

Carries none of the pattern fields, and that is why the criterion is a union rather than one model
with a nullable half. It is also gate-independent: "no customer identifiers leave the account" reads
the same in front of a tool call as in front of a model request.

``model`` is the wire name of one of *this account's* selectable models
(``GET /llm-providers/selectable``), and it is part of the rule rather than platform configuration
because the judge is shown the very content the policy exists to contain. That the account can
actually reach the name is checked when the rule is written — a typo caught here is a 422 on a form,
and the same typo caught at enforcement time is a control that refuses everything it covers.

model.description: Which of this account's models answers it.
model.title: Model

policy.description: What the model is asked to decide, in plain language.
policy.title: Policy

timeout_seconds.description: How long this policy may hold the gate open before it counts as unanswered.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

JudgedCriterionModel.title: JudgedCriterionModel

LLMGatewayRouteMode.description:
How workers reach the gateway for Anthropic-shaped traffic (see the SDK counterpart).

The ``anthropic_`` prefix is the client wire format, not the backend. ``ANTHROPIC_PASSTHROUGH``
(the value when nothing is configured) => the SDK appends ``/anthropic`` and LiteLLM proxies to
real ``api.anthropic.com``. ``ANTHROPIC_TRANSLATE`` => the SDK targets the gateway root so the
client hits LiteLLM's native ``/v1/messages`` translating endpoint, which routes through
``model_list`` to any backend (local Ollama, etc.). The value strings MUST stay in sync with
``komodor_agentops.core.secrets.LLMGatewayRouteMode``.
LLMGatewayRouteMode.title: LLMGatewayRouteMode

LabelItem.description:
One label key/value — a wire pair so the generated client stays a plain model list rather than a
free-form map (the same reason the display/presence responses are lists).
LabelItem.title: LabelItem

LabelSelector.description:
A single ABAC label selector — the ``labels_json`` subset an agent must contain to match (JSONB
``@>``), carried as key/value pairs (keys/values are text).
LabelSelector.title: LabelSelector

LabeledServerRecord.description:
Control-plane view of a server: the tenant-agnostic ``fast_gateway.ServerRecord`` plus this
product's ABAC ``labels`` (#884 Phase D) and its Outpost egress binding. Both live only in the
control-plane ``mcp_servers`` table, so the reusable gateway library/model stays free of them;
this subclass surfaces them on the admin read API without changing the library contract.

allow.description: Glob patterns of tool names to expose (empty = all).
allow.title: Allow

auth.description: Upstream auth scheme. 'oauth' runs FastMCP's browser OAuth flow on first connect and caches tokens persistently.

deny.description: Glob patterns of tool names to hide (wins over allow).
deny.title: Deny

last_check_source.description: What produced the last result, so a stale green is distinguishable from a fresh one.

name.description: Unique name; also used as the mount namespace/prefix. Letters, digits and hyphens only — no underscore (it is the namespace/tool-name separator).
name.title: Name

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client id for the client_credentials grant (not secret).
oauth_client_id.title: Oauth Client Id

oauth_client_secret.description: OAuth client secret as a ${env:VAR} or ${file:path} reference, resolved at connect time. Raw secrets are rejected so the registry never stores one.
oauth_client_secret.title: Oauth Client Secret

oauth_scopes.description: OAuth scopes to request; empty = server/registration default.
oauth_scopes.title: Oauth Scopes

oauth_token_url.description: Token endpoint for the client_credentials grant.
oauth_token_url.title: Oauth Token Url

openapi_config.description: Set when this row is an OpenAPI integration rather than an upstream MCP server: the resolved API base URL and the enabled operations. Null for every ordinary server. Holds no auth material by design, so it is returned unredacted.

outpost_id.description: Egress binding: the Outpost whose tunnel reaches this upstream, or null for a direct dial from the control-plane pod. Surfaced so the admin API can show where a server is reached from; the connect hook re-reads it from the table rather than trusting a record it was handed, since a stripped-to-base ServerRecord would read as unbound — a fail-open.
outpost_id.title: Outpost Id

probe_tool.description: Operator override for the tool a connection test invokes. Null means resolve it — the provider's designation, else a heuristic over the tools the upstream advertises.
probe_tool.title: Probe Tool

provider.description: The catalog provider this upstream is an endpoint of, or null for a hand-registered server no catalog describes. Lets a connection test resolve the probe tool this product ships for a known provider.
provider.title: Provider

static_headers.description: Headers always sent upstream; merged under hook-provided headers. Values may embed ${env:VAR} / ${file:path} secret references resolved at connect time — use those for credentials (e.g. 'Bearer ${env:API_TOKEN}'), because this field is stored in plaintext and returned by the admin read API.
static_headers.title: Static Headers

url.description: Endpoint URL for the upstream MCP server.
url.title: Url

LabeledServerRecord.title: LabeledServerRecord

LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateRequest.description:
One outbound model request, as the parts a criterion reads.

``agent_id`` is optional because not every key names one. An agent normally gets its own virtual key,
minted with LiteLLM's native ``agent_id`` and carried onto the ``UserAPIKeyAuth`` the plugin reads; the
account-wide key belongs to no agent, and is the fallback when minting one did not happen. So a rule
that names agents covers an attributed request and not an unattributed one — the same reading as
``covers_agent``, where an untargeted rule covers both.

Empty lists are a legitimate request (a model call with no system prompt), and they make every
condition on that part false. What a guardrail should do about content it could not read at all is a
separate question, and today's answer is that no rule covers it.
LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateRequest.title: LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateRequest

LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateResponse.description:
``decision`` is ``None`` when no guardrail covers the request — i.e. forward it.

An envelope with a nullable field rather than a bare 200/204 pair, for the same reason as the
tool-call twin: making the allow explicit in a 200 body keeps a failed request from being read as
permission. Anything that is not a 200 must make the plugin refuse the request rather than forward
it, because a guardrail that stops being consulted has stopped being a control.
LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateResponse.title: LlmProxyModelRequestEvaluateResponse

ManualSetupInstructions.description:
Copy-paste fallback for a repo whose hook could not be auto-created (missing App
permission, PAT integration, or no GitHub integration connected at all).
ManualSetupInstructions.title: ManualSetupInstructions

MatchedWorkloadsRequest.title: MatchedWorkloadsRequest

MatchingAgentIds.description:
The agent ids matching one label selector, or one search text — a list rather than a set for the
wire; the twin rebuilds the ``set``. Empty means *nothing matched*: for a label selector the caller
fails closed, for a search text it simply contributes no rows.
MatchingAgentIds.title: MatchingAgentIds

McpCheckKind.description: Which layer of the connection a check exercised.
McpCheckKind.title: McpCheckKind

McpCheckResult.description: One layer's outcome. ``failure`` is set whenever ``status`` is not ``OK``.

tool_name.description: The tool invoked, on the tool-execution check.
tool_name.title: Tool Name

McpCheckResult.title: McpCheckResult

McpCheckSource.description: What produced a recorded health result, so a stale green is distinguishable from a fresh one.
McpCheckSource.title: McpCheckSource

McpFailureKind.description:
Why a check failed or was skipped, coarse enough to drive different UI and remediation.

The distinction that matters most to an operator is ``AUTH`` (the credential is valid but the
upstream refuses the action — fix scopes/permissions) versus ``NETWORK``/``TIMEOUT`` (we never
got a usable answer — fix reachability). Classifying here rather than in the browser keeps the
exception object, which is the only place the difference is reliably visible.
McpFailureKind.title: McpFailureKind

McpServerOutpostBinding.description:
Which Outpost's tunnel reaches an upstream (``docs/prds/outpost.md``).

A pure locality fact — it carries no credential and no credential reference, because the Outpost
never holds the upstream's secret: the control plane attaches it before the request enters the
tunnel, exactly as it does on a direct dial.
McpServerOutpostBinding.title: McpServerOutpostBinding

McpServerOutpostUpdate.description:
Bind an upstream's egress to one Outpost. Locality only — no credential field, deliberately:
binding changes which network path reaches the server, never how it authenticates.
McpServerOutpostUpdate.title: McpServerOutpostUpdate

MissingToolNamesResponse.description:
The subset of the requested tool names absent from the scoped account's catalog. A list rather
than a set on the wire; the twin rebuilds the port's set.
MissingToolNamesResponse.title: MissingToolNamesResponse

ModelOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
ModelOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: ModelOnboardingCompletionResponse

ModelRequestPart.description:
Which part of an outbound model request a condition reads.

A closed set, unlike gate #1's free-form argument name: a tool's arguments are the tool author's
vocabulary and we cannot enumerate them, while a model request has a shape every provider shares.
Naming the part is what keeps a rule meaning one thing — "no card numbers in what the user sent" and
"no card numbers anywhere in the request" are different controls, and a criterion that silently meant
the wider one would over-refuse.

``SYSTEM`` is separate from ``MESSAGES`` because the two differ in who wrote them: a system prompt is
the operator's own text, message content is whatever reached the agent. A jailbreak rule pointed at
everything would fire on the system prompt that describes what to refuse.
ModelRequestPart.title: ModelRequestPart

ModelRequestPatternCriterionModel.description:
One deterministic predicate over a model request's content — gate #3's counterpart to
:class:`PatternCriterionModel`, with ``conditions`` in place of tool globs since a model request has
no tool name to match.

``conditions`` is non-empty by contract, and the reason is sharper than at gate #1: a tool-call
criterion is anchored by its tool patterns, so dropping its conditions widens it to the tool, while a
model-request criterion has no such anchor and would cover the account's entire LLM traffic.

``variant`` is tagged distinctly from :class:`PatternCriterionModel` (``content_pattern`` rather than
``pattern``) so the two shapes can share one discriminated union on the wire; both are
``CriterionVariant.PATTERN`` underneath, which is why the gate — not the tag — is what decides which
of them a guardrail may hold.
ModelRequestPatternCriterionModel.title: ModelRequestPatternCriterionModel

ModuleKey.description:
The product modules a workflow definition can belong to.

A closed set rather than free text: a module's deterministic step handlers are registered by
``(module_key, step_key)``, so a typo'd key would silently register a handler nothing dispatches.
ModuleKey.title: ModuleKey

NotificationSinkEventFilter.description: One entry in a sink's ``subscribed_events`` list (architecture doc §2 "Event filter shape").
NotificationSinkEventFilter.title: NotificationSinkEventFilter

NotificationSinkKind.description:
A sink's transport. ``https`` is the only kind this MVP ships; ``slack``/``msteams`` are named
now (per the architecture doc §1) so the ``kind`` discriminator and its CHECK constraint don't need
a migration when a second kind actually lands — only its ``render()``/``send()`` pair and
``config_json`` shape are new work then.
NotificationSinkKind.title: NotificationSinkKind

NotificationSinkWithSecretResponse.description: Returned only on create and rotate-secret — exposes the plaintext signing secret once.
NotificationSinkWithSecretResponse.title: NotificationSinkWithSecretResponse

OAuthStatusResponse.description:
Where a server's interactive sign-in has got to — and nothing else.

It used to carry a ``degraded`` flag as well, read from a set the gateway kept in memory. That
made this route the only place a connection problem surfaced, which is why the failure badge
could only ever appear on an OAuth server; and being per-pod, the answer depended on which
replica served the request. Health is now on the server row, where every replica reads the same
one and every auth mode has it — so it is read from there instead of from here.
OAuthStatusResponse.title: OAuthStatusResponse

OnboardingChecklistResponse.description:
The whole checklist for one account and one caller.

Steps the caller may not see, and steps not relevant to this account yet, are **absent** rather
than flagged — so `total` is the denominator for this caller and this account, not a global
count, and `completed`/`total` always agree with the rows above them.
OnboardingChecklistResponse.title: OnboardingChecklistResponse

OnboardingSummaryResponse.description:
Counts only — what the header badge needs.

A separate endpoint because the badge renders on every page: it wants "how many are left", not
twelve rows, and shipping the tree to answer that would make the checklist's cost proportional
to navigation. Same probes and the same cache underneath, so the two can't disagree.
OnboardingSummaryResponse.title: OnboardingSummaryResponse

OnboardingTaskResponse.description:
One activation step as the caller sees it.

Deliberately free of anything a surface would have to interpret: no probe, no flag, no
capability, no event topics. Everything a step needs to render — its label, where it goes, how
far along it is, what to ask the assistant — is on the row, so a new step reaches every surface
without a frontend change. `status` is computed on read; a step is never *told* it is done.
OnboardingTaskResponse.title: OnboardingTaskResponse

OpenApiConfig.description: The server row's OpenAPI half: where to call, and which operations exist as tools.

base_url.description: The resolved, validated API base URL the generated tools call.
base_url.title: Base Url

base_url_override.description: What the operator typed, if they overrode the document's own servers[] entry. Kept for audit and the UI.
base_url_override.title: Base Url Override

enabled_operations.description: The operations exposed as tools. One explicit list: there is no null-means-all and no exclude list, so an operation that appears in the document after import stays off until a human enables it.
enabled_operations.title: Enabled Operations

OpenApiConfig.title: OpenApiConfig

OpenApiConfigureRequest.description:
Re-selecting operations, re-writing notes, or re-pointing the base URL.

The spec URL is not settable here: it is the row's ``url`` and identifies the integration. Point at
a different document by creating a different integration.

``base_url_override`` distinguishes absent from null, through ``model_fields_set``: omitting it keeps
the stored override, and an explicit ``null`` clears it. A default of ``None`` alone would make every
caller that does not mention the field re-point the integration, credential attached.
OpenApiConfigureRequest.title: OpenApiConfigureRequest

credential_source.description: 'credential' or 'integration', or null for no injected auth.
credential_source.title: Credential Source

name.description: The server name, which namespaces the generated tools.
name.title: Name

base_url_override.description: Call the API at this base instead of the one the document declares.
base_url_override.title: Base Url Override

spec_url.description: The OpenAPI document to read. Fetched through the egress guard, so a public HTTPS URL.
spec_url.title: Spec Url

OpenApiDiscoverResponse.description: What the document turned out to contain, before anything is persisted.
OpenApiDiscoverResponse.title: OpenApiDiscoverResponse

warning.description: Set when the write succeeded but the mounted tool set could not be re-introspected. The stored configuration is authoritative, it is what the dial compiles, but the catalog still advertises the previous tools until the next reload.
warning.title: Warning

OperationSelection.description: One operation an operator asked to enable, with the note they wrote for it.
OperationSelection.title: OperationSelection

OptimizationPreset.description:
One named preset's full field set — the shape ``GET /policies/defaults`` returns for each
of the four presets, distinct from :class:`Policy` (no ``name``/``priority``/``scopes``, and
``guard_rails``/``percentile`` are required here rather than optional).
OptimizationPreset.title: OptimizationPreset

OptimizeOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
OptimizeOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: OptimizeOnboardingCompletionResponse

host.description: Exact DNS name or IP, or one leading `*.` label (`*.internal.example.com` matches `a.internal.example.com`, never `internal.example.com` itself and never `a.b.internal.example.com`). Compared label-wise after normalization; a rule with an embedded `*` is a configuration error, not a broader match.
host.title: Host

path_prefix.description: Permitted path prefix, matched on segment boundaries. Absent means any path under this host and port -- which is broader than most upstreams need, so it is worth setting.
path_prefix.title: Path Prefix

port.description: The exact port. No range, no default: a rule that quietly meant 443 would be a rule the operator did not write.
port.title: Port

scheme.description: The only scheme this rule permits. Explicit rather than defaulted, so allowing plaintext to a private host is something an operator wrote down.

OutpostConfigDrift.description: What the reported digests say about a deployment, relative to what AgentOps rendered.
OutpostConfigDrift.title: OutpostConfigDrift

OutpostCredential.description:
A credential value, returned once and never again.

``hint`` is the first and last four characters, which is what a list view can safely show later so an
operator can tell two saved values apart. Nothing else about the value is ever persisted in a form
that can be read back.
OutpostCredential.title: OutpostCredential

OutpostDetail.description: The single-Outpost view: everything the list shows, plus the declared allowlist.
OutpostDetail.title: OutpostDetail

OutpostInstall.description:
What an operator needs to run the relay: the chart, the values, and the commands that apply them.

Rendered from the declaration plus the upstreams bound to this Outpost, so an operator never
hand-writes the local allowlist. Identical on every read — there is nothing here that exists only
once, because the credential is deliberately not part of it.

Two commands, each with its own document, because installing and upgrading want opposite things
from Helm. A first install has nothing to preserve and everything to state; an upgrade must keep
every value the operator added themselves, which the install command would replace.
OutpostInstall.title: OutpostInstall

OutpostStatus.description:
Lifecycle of the *declaration*, not of the tunnel. ``PENDING`` is a created Outpost that has
never completed a handshake; ``ENROLLED`` is one that has. Whether it is reachable *right now* is
presence, read from ``outpost_instances`` — never from this column, which would go stale the
moment a pod died.
OutpostStatus.title: OutpostStatus

OutpostSummary.description:
One Outpost as the list view sees it: the declaration, plus what presence currently observes.

The declared and the observed halves are deliberately adjacent, because the operator's question is
always the difference between them — a ``status`` of ``enrolled`` with ``connected`` false is a relay
that used to work, which is a completely different problem from one that never enrolled.
OutpostSummary.title: OutpostSummary

OutpostUpstreamsResponse.description:
The upstreams bound to one Outpost. Carries no credential and no credential reference — the
Outpost is told which hosts it must reach, never how to authenticate to them (the control plane
attaches the upstream's secret before the request enters the tunnel).
OutpostUpstreamsResponse.title: OutpostUpstreamsResponse

OverviewCoverage.description:
Coverage = repos bound to an *active* workflow whose webhook is healthy, over the repos the
connected GitHub App can see. ``integration_repos`` is ``None`` when no App integration is
connected (the denominator is then unknown, not zero). A repo on an active workflow with an
``error``/``pending`` webhook is silently unreviewed, so it counts as NOT covered and is named
in ``unhealthy_repos``.
OverviewCoverage.title: OverviewCoverage

OverviewEvaluator.description:
An evaluator's activity in the window, with the all-time `first_evaluated_at` that makes a
newly added one recognisable as new.

That flag is the point of this list: a new evaluator's numbers are not yet comparable to an
incumbent's, so a fleet average that dropped the week one was added needs to be read as "a
stricter evaluator arrived", not "the agents got worse". `avg_score` spans whatever rubrics this
evaluator was asked for, so it is a volume-and-recency signal rather than a quality
measurement — compare evaluators on a shared rubric via `rubrics`, not on this number.
OverviewEvaluator.title: OverviewEvaluator

OverviewRubricStat.description:
One rubric's headline over the window: its average and how much evaluating produced it.

`evals` counts verdicts and `graded_runs` counts distinct runs; they differ whenever a panel of
several evaluators scores the same rubric, and the average is over verdicts.
OverviewRubricStat.title: OverviewRubricStat

OverviewTrendPoint.description:
One day in the reviews-over-time series. ``date`` is ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (UTC). ``spend_usd`` is
the day's summed pass cost, or None when no pass that day recorded a cost — the chart gaps
honestly rather than plotting a fake $0 (a day with reviews but no cost data is different from
a day that cost nothing). The ``findings_*`` counts are an ACTIVITY measure — what the passes
that ran that day reported — unlike the totals, which are the open-set (latest pass per PR).
OverviewTrendPoint.title: OverviewTrendPoint

OverviewValueEstimate.description:
The modelled engineer-time-returned figure, with every input named so the UI can render the
arithmetic. ``*_minutes`` are the platform-default constants (per-finding triage time by
severity, and a per-PR first-pass triage credit); the ``*_count``/``*_minutes_total`` pairs let
the card show "7 high × 25m = 175m" for each line.
OverviewValueEstimate.title: OverviewValueEstimate

PatternCriterionModel.description:
One predicate decided by comparing text: which tools, and optionally which arguments.

A criterion decides nothing on its own — the gate, the audience and the action belong to the
guardrail. **Any** criterion matching means the guardrail applies, while the conditions *within* one
criterion must all hold, so an either/or is two criteria and a narrowing is two conditions.
PatternCriterionModel.title: PatternCriterionModel

add_node_affinity_to_marked_pods.title: Add Node Affinity To Marked Pods

Policy.description:
Mirrors Komodor's ``RightSizingMultiScopePolicy`` — the same shape for a create/update
request body and the policy embedded in every read response.
Policy.title: Policy

PolicyAction.description: Actions a policy rule can prescribe.
PolicyAction.title: PolicyAction

PolicyCondition.description: A single condition evaluated against execution context.
PolicyCondition.title: PolicyCondition

PolicyDefaults.description:
Default settings applied when no rule matches.

The first four fields are language/runtime budgets evaluated by the
rule engine. The remaining fields are **sandbox resource constraints**
consumed by sandbox providers (Azure, Docker, Hyperlight) and are
ignored by the rule engine itself.

max_cpu.description: Sandbox CPU limit in vCPUs (e.g. 0.5, 1.0). None = provider default.
max_cpu.title: Max Cpu

max_memory_mb.description: Sandbox memory limit in MiB. None = provider default.
max_memory_mb.title: Max Memory Mb

network_default.description: Default sandbox egress action when a host is not on network_allowlist. 'deny' is fail-closed and is the default. Set to 'allow' only for trusted dev/research workloads.
network_default.title: Network Default

timeout_seconds.description: Per-execute_code wall-clock cap. None = provider default.
timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds

PolicyDefaults.title: PolicyDefaults

inherit.description: If false, parent governance.yaml files are not loaded (stops inheritance)
inherit.title: Inherit

network_allowlist.description: Host patterns the sandbox may reach (e.g. 'pypi.org', '*.github.com'). Combined with defaults.network_default to form the sandbox egress policy.
network_allowlist.title: Network Allowlist

scope.description: Glob pattern — policy only applies when action path matches
scope.title: Scope

tool_allowlist.description: Tool names the agent may invoke. Enforced host-side by the PolicyEvaluator before any sandbox call.
tool_allowlist.title: Tool Allowlist

PolicyGrantInput.description:
A subjectless member grant a policy bundles: a single capability with its scope. No subject/role
(that is a binding grant) and no id/effect on input (effect is allow-only for v1).
PolicyGrantInput.title: PolicyGrantInput

PolicyListRow.description:
A summary projection, not the full policy — no ``scopes``/``guardRails``. ``cluster_name``
is a deprecated V1 artifact on Komodor's side (superseded by multi-scope ``scopes``); kept here
since Komodor's own comment says it's retained for backward compatibility, not that it's always
empty.
PolicyListRow.title: PolicyListRow

PolicyResponse.description:
``GetMultiScopePolicyResponse`` — returned by get-by-id, create, and update alike (the
latter two via Komodor's shared ``SendPolicyResponse`` helper); create/update just differ in
HTTP status, not shape.
PolicyResponse.title: PolicyResponse

PolicyRule.description: A single governance rule within a policy document.

override.description: If true, replaces a parent rule with the same name during folder-level merge
override.title: Override

priority.description: Higher priority rules are evaluated first
priority.title: Priority

PolicyRule.title: PolicyRule

PreviousVersionInfo.description:
The one-level rollback snapshot's metadata (not the rendered values themselves),
surfaced on the response so the UI can label a "Revert to previous version" action.
PreviousVersionInfo.title: PreviousVersionInfo

ProvisionAccountRequest.description:
Body for the provision endpoint. ``credential_ref`` is the agent's chosen LLM credential; the
gateway is provisioned only when it selects the managed token (``model`` decides).
ProvisionAccountRequest.title: ProvisionAccountRequest

QualityOverview.description:
The Quality Lab Overview: what was evaluated in the window, how each rubric is trending, which
agents moved, and who did the evaluating.

Counts are of LLM verdicts only — a human grade is one person's spot check, not a measurement
this view trends. Every filter (`rubric`, `agent_id`, `evaluator_id`) narrows the whole response
together, so the tiles always describe the same slice the chart is drawing.
QualityOverview.title: QualityOverview

RecordSyncRequest.description:
What an install reports about itself when a reconcile pass finishes. Never its install id —
that comes from the credential, so a compromised key cannot mark another install as healthy.

namespace.description: The namespace the operator runs in, which binds it to this account.
namespace.title: Namespace

RecordSyncRequest.title: RecordSyncRequest

ResolveOutcomeKind.description:
The three terminal shapes resolving a presented credential can take — the wire discriminator on
the resolve endpoint's response and the tag on :class:`ResolutionOutcome`.
ResolveOutcomeKind.title: ResolveOutcomeKind

ResolveWorkerConfigRequest.description:
Body for the worker-config resolve endpoint. The account is never a body field — it is the
authenticated identity's (the calling worker's own), taken from ``_scoped_account_id()``.
ResolveWorkerConfigRequest.title: ResolveWorkerConfigRequest

ResourceOwnershipState.description:
Who declares a resource, from the asking install's point of view.

Three states rather than an owner reference the caller compares itself against, because the
comparison is the whole question and every caller would make it the same way.
ResourceOwnershipState.title: ResourceOwnershipState

ResourceOwnershipView.description:
The answer to "does this install declare this resource", plus what a conflict message needs.

Deliberately carries no ``install_id`` for another install and no ``uid`` for any: the owner's
display name and cluster coordinates are what a rejection already tells anyone who attempts a
write, and a reconciler needs nothing further to word its own condition.
ResourceOwnershipView.title: ResourceOwnershipView

ResourceScope.description:
One entry in a policy's ``scopes`` list. Every field is optional — Komodor's own struct has
no required field here; an empty scope matches nothing, which is a valid (if useless) policy.
ResourceScope.title: ResourceScope

ResponseConditionModel.description:
One condition on what a tool returned — gate #2's counterpart to :class:`ArgConditionModel`, and the
only one of the three with **no subject** to name. A tool call has arguments the tool's author named and
a model request has parts distinguished by who wrote them; a tool response is one thing, the text the
agent is about to read.
ResponseConditionModel.title: ResponseConditionModel

ReviewRunSummary.description:
One ``review_runs`` row — the full per-push dispatch history for a review (unlike
``ReviewerRunResult``, which collapses to the latest run per reviewer agent).

``run_status`` and ``parse_error`` are what make a pass that produced no verdict legible: a run
that failed outright and a run that succeeded while breaking the structured-output contract both
leave ``verdict`` null, and they call for different action. Optional only for shape reasons — a
foreign key ties every row to a live run, so in practice it is always populated.
ReviewRunSummary.title: ReviewRunSummary

RevisionArtifactCategory.description: High-level definition area a changed artifact belongs to.
RevisionArtifactCategory.title: RevisionArtifactCategory

RightSizingStatsRequest.description: Clean documented contract — same reasoning as ``AllocationStatsRequest``.
RightSizingStatsRequest.title: RightSizingStatsRequest

active_cpu_cores_hours_diff_down.title: Active Cpu Cores Hours Diff Down

active_memory_gib_hours_diff_down.title: Active Memory Gib Hours Diff Down

automated_available_savings_cpu_cores_ho.title: Automated Available Savings Cpu Cores Hours

automated_available_savings_memory_gib_h.title: Automated Available Savings Memory Gib Hours

memory_request_mib_active_limits_recomme.title: Memory Request Mib Active Limits Recommendation

memory_request_mib_active_requests_recom.title: Memory Request Mib Active Requests Recommendation

active_fixed_under_provisioned_cpu_cores.title: Active Fixed Under Provisioned Cpu Cores

active_fixed_under_provisioned_memory_mi.title: Active Fixed Under Provisioned Memory Mib

active_fixed_under_provisioned_resources.title: Active Fixed Under Provisioned Resources Score

RubricAverage.description:
One rubric's auto-grade average over a window, with how many runs it covers.

Rubrics are not interchangeable measurements, so they are reported side by side and never
averaged together: the mean of `precision 0.98` and `safety 0.35` is a number no evaluator
asserted, and it moves with how many rubrics a rule happens to ask for.
RubricAverage.title: RubricAverage

RubricExtremes.description:
An agent's best and worst runs on one rubric.

The two lists are what turn "averaging 0.62 on safety" into "read this specific run" — an average
tells you something is wrong, and only a run tells you what. Per rubric because a run can be the
agent's best on `precision` and its worst on `safety`, and a combined ranking would show neither.
Both are empty when the agent has fewer runs graded on this rubric than there are slots to fill,
which is common and not an error.
RubricExtremes.title: RubricExtremes

RubricSeries.description:
One rubric's daily averages, oldest first. Days with no verdict are omitted rather than
zero-filled: a gap is missing data, and plotting it as 0.0 would invent a catastrophic score.
RubricSeries.title: RubricSeries

RunAgentMapResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the twin rebuilds
the ``{run_id -> agent_id}`` dict.
RunAgentMapResponse.title: RunAgentMapResponse

RunQualityRow.description:
A run paired with its human quality score, for the per-agent
sort/filter-by-score list ("worst runs and why" in one click). `avg_score` is
null for an ungraded run; `rationale`/`reviewer`/`scored_at` come from the
most recent score on the run.
RunQualityRow.title: RunQualityRow

RunSummariesResponse.description:
A list rather than a map so the generated client stays a plain model list; the twin rebuilds the
``{run_id -> RunSummary}`` dict from each run's own id.
RunSummariesResponse.title: RunSummariesResponse

RunUsage.description:
Token and cost accounting for a run, or for a single ``token.created`` event.

The three input counts are **disjoint** — a token is billed exactly once, at exactly one rate, so
``input_tokens`` is the FRESH input only and the two cache counts sit beside it rather than inside
it. Summing them into one field is what makes a cost estimate wrong by an order of magnitude for a
prompt-caching agent: a cache read costs a tenth of fresh input, so pricing reads at the fresh rate
overstates a cache-heavy run's cost roughly 10x. See ``runtime/usage/pricing.py`` for the rates.
RunUsage.title: RunUsage

RuntimeOnboardingCompletionResponse.description:
The ``{visible, done}`` completion of this component's activation steps for the scoped account,
plus the query cost measured owner-side. A per-component model name (not a shared one) so each
owner's ``/onboarding`` endpoint has a distinct OpenAPI schema.
RuntimeOnboardingCompletionResponse.title: RuntimeOnboardingCompletionResponse

ScopeException.description:
The full record — what create/update/list return, adding ``id`` and audit fields on top of
the request shape. Never carries ``accountId``/``accountName`` — Komodor's own response mapper
drops them even though the DB row has them.
ScopeException.title: ScopeException

ScopeExceptionItemResponse.description:
``PolicyScopeExceptionWorkloadItemResponse`` — create/update's response envelope.
``warnings`` carries e.g. ``WORKLOAD_NOT_IN_SUMMARY`` when the workload has no recommendation
data yet; present only when Komodor actually has something to warn about.
ScopeExceptionItemResponse.title: ScopeExceptionItemResponse

ScopeExceptionListResponse.description:
Offset/limit pagination (``{limit, offset, total}``) — a different style than the
token-based pagination the allocation/right-sizing routes use; Komodor's own choice per
endpoint, mirrored rather than normalized.
ScopeExceptionListResponse.title: ScopeExceptionListResponse

ScopeExceptionRequest.description:
Request body for both create (``POST``) and update (``PUT``) — Komodor uses the same DTO
for both.
ScopeExceptionRequest.title: ScopeExceptionRequest

ScorePoint.description:
One day of one rubric's series. `evals` is the day's volume, which is what stops a single
verdict's 0.2 from reading like a trend.
ScorePoint.title: ScorePoint

ScoreValue.description:
A score's value, typed. `numeric` is the canonical **0..1 float** (H1.1
re-base) for both `numeric` ratings (human 1-5 stars map (n-1)/4 → 0..1; the LLM
evaluator writes a continuous 0..1) and `boolean` (0 or 1); `label` holds a short
categorical value. 0..1 is the one scale that fits 1-5, 0-100%, and thumbs alike.
ScoreValue.title: ScoreValue

ScorecardRubric.description:
An agent's average on one rubric, and how many of its runs were graded on it.

The scorecard's unit of meaning. A rubric name is comparable across evaluators and across time —
"is this agent getting safer" is answerable — which is what an average over a single evaluator
never was, since each evaluator measures something different.
ScorecardRubric.title: ScorecardRubric

ServerAuth.description:
Upstream authentication scheme used when connecting to a registered server.

``oauth`` is the interactive browser authorization-code flow (Mode B only);
``oauth_client_credentials`` is the headless machine-to-machine grant. Static
token / API-key auth needs no scheme: put a ``${env:}``/``${file:}`` secret
reference in ``static_headers`` and it resolves at connect time.
ServerAuth.title: ServerAuth

ServerConfigProbeRequest.description: An unsaved server's address, for the pre-create reachability check.
ServerConfigProbeRequest.title: ServerConfigProbeRequest

ServerConfigProbeResponse.description:
What can be learned about an upstream from its address alone, before it is saved.

Deliberately NOT a ``ServerTestResponse``: no credential is attached yet (the binding is keyed on
a server id that does not exist), so this can prove reachability and read the tool list but says
nothing about permissions. Keeping it a different shape stops it being mistaken for the real
two-layer verdict.

reachable.description: Whether the server answered at all. A 401 counts as reachable: the address is right and something is serving MCP there, it just wants credentials.
reachable.title: Reachable

requires_auth.description: The server answered but refused the request unauthenticated — expected for most providers.
requires_auth.title: Requires Auth

suggested_probe_tool.description: Which tool the automatic selection would call, so the UI names the same one the test will.
suggested_probe_tool.title: Suggested Probe Tool

ServerConfigProbeResponse.title: ServerConfigProbeResponse

ServerRefreshResponse.description:
What a refresh did, in one shape for both kinds of server row.

``updated`` and ``dropped`` are empty for an ordinary MCP upstream, which has no stored selection
to drop from, so a caller renders what it is given instead of asking what kind of row this was.

dropped.description: 'METHOD /path' for each enabled operation the document no longer declares.
dropped.title: Dropped

failure.description: Why the upstream could not be re-read. The row keeps serving its last known tools.
failure.title: Failure

updated.description: Tool names whose generated shape changed upstream.
updated.title: Updated

ServerRefreshResponse.title: ServerRefreshResponse

ServerTestResponse.description:
The result of testing one upstream.

``ok`` / ``tool_count`` / ``error`` describe the connectivity layer and predate the nested
checks; they are kept so existing callers keep working, and because "did the handshake work"
remains the single most useful summary. ``checks`` is the full picture.
ServerTestResponse.title: ServerTestResponse

SigningCredentialRef.description: Reference to the credential a webhook validates against (never the secret value).
SigningCredentialRef.title: SigningCredentialRef

SkillQualityRollup.description:
Per-skill quality over a window. `avg_score` pools two honest signals (M5):
DIRECT offline skill grades and the human grades on runs that USED the skill
(correlational — "runs using this skill rate X", not a causal claim). A run is
attributed to a skill via its `agentops.skill.invoke` telemetry, matched on
skill_id; unknown skill usage is excluded, never guessed. `attributed_runs`
counts the distinct runs that contributed; `direct_count` the offline grades.
The auto-grade (H1) signal is kept separate from the human numbers and reported
per rubric in `llm_by_rubric`; `avg_llm_score` is the lowest rubric's average,
named in `avg_llm_rubric` (see `AgentQualityRollup` for why the lowest and not a
mean). Null/0/empty when there are no auto-grades.
SkillQualityRollup.title: SkillQualityRollup

SlackChannelTriggerResponse.description:
A ``slack_channel`` trigger row — the agent's declared Slack channel subscription.

Always agent-spec-sourced (declared in ``agent-spec.yaml``, synced on heartbeat), so it is
read-only in the UI. ``channels`` are normalized Slack channel NAMES (lowercase, no ``#``).
SlackChannelTriggerResponse.title: SlackChannelTriggerResponse

SpecBudget.description:
What the structural budget measured, so an operator can see how close a document came.

Reported by discover for exactly that reason. **No UI renders it today**, it is
returned because a refusal that cannot be explained is a support ticket, and its shape is pinned
here (and asserted in the ingest tests) so a field rename cannot pass unnoticed on the way to a
consumer that does not exist yet.
SpecBudget.title: SpecBudget

StepOverrideRequest.description:
The one thing a template instantiation may customize per step in v1: which specialists it
binds. Everything else about a step (goal, schemas, duration) comes from the template.
StepOverrideRequest.title: StepOverrideRequest

StepType.description:
How a step executes.

``ORCHESTRATED`` dispatches the generic step-orchestrator agent with the step's bound specialist
allowlist. ``DETERMINISTIC`` invokes a control-plane handler registered by ``(module_key,
step_key)`` — no agent, no LLM, no ``runs`` row — for steps that are pure bookkeeping.
``HUMAN_DECISION`` is engine-owned waiting: it parks the run on a question and resumes on the
operator's answer, again with no agent and no run.

Only the first dispatches an agent, which is why ``module_workflow_step_runs.run_id`` is
nullable for the other two.
StepType.title: StepType

SubscribeRequest.description:
Add a subscription to a sink.

``target_id=None`` creates a wildcard subscription ("all sources of this ``target_type``
in the account") — see architecture doc §2.
SubscribeRequest.title: SubscribeRequest

SuiteRegressionsResponse.description:
One suite's regression sweep. `alerts` alone cannot be read as a verdict: `ungraded_runs`
(completed runs nothing scored), `failed_runs` (runs that never completed) and
`scenarios_without_baseline` (members with too little scored history to compare) say how much of
the suite the sweep could actually see. A suite whose every run failed reports no alerts and no
ungraded runs — `failed_runs` is what separates it from a suite nobody has run.
